roster.title: Roster
roster.subtitle: Build the monthly shift roster — pick a month, then assign shifts across your team.
roster.noCompanies: No companies in your scope to roster.
roster.shiftHint: A shift ending at or before its start crosses midnight (⊕). The schedule drives attendance OT; no roster falls back to the company policy.
roster.varianceHint: Rostered shifts that didn't go to plan — no-shows, late starts, short hours, or rest days worked.
roster.noEmployees: No active employees in this company.
roster.createShiftFirst: Create a shift above to start rostering.
roster.noRestWarningHint: Seven days in a row with a shift and no rest day — EA 1955 s.59 requires one rest day per week.
roster.bankInLieuConsentPrompt: This employee is within the First Schedule (statutory overtime pay applies). Banking time in lieu instead of the statutory cash premium needs the employee's explicit prior agreement. Confirm consent to proceed?
roster.multiBreakStorageHint: Multiple break windows are saved and shown, but the hours deducted still use their combined total — per-break precision is a future enhancement.
roster.generated: Roster generated for {employees} employees — {working} working-day and {rest} rest-day entries.
roster.generateHint: Fills every date in the range from the shift's weekly pattern: shift entries on working days and explicit rest days on the rest, so the company policy never silently overrides the pattern. Re-running overwrites the same dates.
roster.manageShiftsHint: Shift schedules are managed in Shift settings; a person's usual shift is set on their profile as their Default shift. Use the roster for date-specific exceptions.
roster.copyHint: Copies every shift and rest day from the source dates onto the target, keeping each day's position. Re-running overwrites the same target dates.
roster.copiedDone: Copied {rows} roster entries onto the target dates.
roster.copiedEmpty: No roster entries found in the source dates to copy.
roster.ghostHint: Grey = the employee's usual shift filling a date nothing was rostered on.
roster.templateNotesTitle: How to fill in this roster
roster.templateNoteBlank: Leave a cell blank to keep that date exactly as it is.
roster.templateNoteCode: Type a shift code to roster that shift on that date.
roster.templateNoteRd: Type RD for a rostered rest day.
roster.templateNoteOff: Type OFF to remove any entry for that date.
roster.templateNoteMonth: Only dates inside {month} are saved — any other date column is reported and ignored.
roster.templateFailed: Could not build the template file.
roster.viewOnly: A supervisor views the roster; an HR Administrator changes it.
roster.pastConfirm: {count, plural, =1 {# date is} other {# dates are}} today or earlier and may already have been attended. Change anyway?
roster.rowConfirm: Set {count, plural, =1 {# date} other {# dates}} for this employee?
roster.rowEditHint: Tick the dates, choose one shift, then apply. Each date is filed in the Audit Trail with the shift before and after.
roster.applyRow: Apply to {count, plural, =1 {# date} other {# dates}}

import.title: Upload Shift Roster
import.description: Download the month, type the shift codes, and send it back. Nothing is saved until you have seen what will change.
import.dropHere: Choose a file or drop it here
import.uploadHint: Excel or CSV. Only dates inside {month} are saved.
import.vocabularyTitle: What to type in a cell
import.vocabBlank: Blank — leave that date exactly as it is.
import.vocabBracket: A code in brackets, like (MB28) — also left as it is. That is how an exported month marks a day covered only by the usual shift.
import.vocabOff: OFF or a dash — remove any entry for that date.
import.save: Save {count, plural, =0 {no changes} =1 {# change} other {# changes}}
import.savedCount: {count, plural, =1 {# roster day saved} other {# roster days saved}}
import.outsideMonthNote: Only {month} was read. Any column for {prev}, {next} or any other month is listed above and was not saved.
import.reasonUnknownEmployee: No active employee with that number in your scope
import.reasonMissingEmployeeNo: No employee number on this line
import.reasonOutOfMonth: Date is outside the chosen month
import.reasonBadDateColumn: That column heading is not a real date
import.reasonDuplicate: The same employee and date appears earlier in the file
import.unsupportedFileType: That file type is not supported — use .xlsx, .xls or .csv.
import.emptySheet: The first sheet of that workbook is empty.

roster.totalNormalHoursNormalHint: Worked out from your times and breaks. Change it if a normal day on this shift is a different length.
roster.totalNormalHoursSemiHint: Required on a Semi Flexi shift. Overtime starts once this many hours of work have been done, breaks not counted.
roster.breakFixedHint: Fixed means the break is taken at that clock time. Untick it and the employee takes the break whenever they like.
roster.breakFixedLockedHint: Every break on this shift is flexible, so Fixed cannot be ticked: the break is an allowance the employee may take at any time, not a clock time to be kept.
roster.breakRowMinutesHint: On a flexible break you can set how many minutes it is worth. Leave it blank and the break is counted the way it is today — only the minutes the employee was actually away inside those times.
roster.dailyCutoffHint: Any clocking after this time counts towards the next day. Leave it off and the system keeps deciding that on its own, as it does today.
roster.halfDayCutoffHint: Clock out before this time and the day is treated as a half day.
roster.halfDayCutoffDerived: Worked out for you — half of {total} is {half} of work, breaks not counted (about {at}).
roster.halfDayCutoffDerivedPending: Worked out for you once the total normal working hours are set.
roster.dayKindHint: Full is an ordinary working day. Half is a working day with half the normal hours. Rest is the statutory rest day. Off is a non-working day that is not the rest day.
roster.flexibleBreakUse: Let employees take their break at any time
roster.flexibleBreakHint: With this on, the allowed minutes come off every worked day whether or not the employee took the break inside the times above — those times stay as guidance. It changes how hours are counted for this shift, so it is off until you turn it on.
roster.breakDeductionSummary: {deducted} comes off a full day, leaving {net} of normal working time.
roster.breakDeductionSemiHint: On a Semi Flexi shift the normal working time is the figure set above, not the window, so no total is worked out here.
roster.moreSettingsHint: Description, category, day type, earliest clock-in, latest clock-out, 2nd half-day clock-in, full-day leave, full-day overtime, normal-hours rounding, the overtime schedule and the shift premium — all still saved, all still editable.
roster.pickCompanyToEdit: Choose a company above to generate, copy or upload a roster.
roster.exceptionsNone: Nothing went off plan in this month.
roster.pastWarning: {count, plural, =1 {# ticked date is} other {# ticked dates are}} today or earlier and may already have been attended.
roster.rowEditMissing: That employee is not on this roster.
roster.rowEditNoDates: Tick at least one date before applying.
roster.rangeCapHint: Up to {days} days can be shown at once.
roster.rangeTooWide: A date range can cover at most {days} days, and that one asked for {asked}. Showing the first {days} days.
roster.rangeBackwards: The To date is before the From date. Showing the From date on its own.

databaseError.duplicate: This would create a duplicate of a record that already exists. Reference {ref}.
databaseError.linked: This record is still linked to other records, so it cannot be changed or removed this way. Reference {ref}.
databaseError.invalidValue: One of the values entered is not allowed here. Reference {ref}.
databaseError.rule: This change was refused by a safeguard that protects existing records, such as a closed payroll. Reference {ref}.
databaseError.busy: The system was busy and the change was not completed. Please try again. Reference {ref}.

dashboard.noHires: No hires in the last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
dashboard.inDays: in {d, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
dashboard.joinedDaysAgo: joined {d, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
dashboard.joinedWeeksAgo: joined {w, plural, one {# week} other {# weeks}} ago
dashboard.joinedMonthsAgo: joined {m, plural, one {# month} other {# months}} ago
dashboard.daysRemaining: {cat, select, one {{v} day} other {{v} days}} remaining
dashboard.customizeHint: Add, remove, or drag to reorder your cards, then save your layout.
dashboard.mandatoryCardMessage: This dashboard card is mandatory and cannot be removed.
dashboard.mandatoryCardHint: Mandatory — set by HR, cannot be removed.
dashboard.shortcutsRowHint: Up to {max}. Drag a card, or focus its handle and press Space then the arrow keys, to change the order.
dashboard.shortcutsEmptyHint: No shortcuts yet. Use Add Card to pick up to {max}.
dashboard.shortcutsLimitHint: You already have {max} shortcuts. Remove one to add another.
dashboard.shortcutsLimitToast: You can show at most {max} shortcuts. Remove one first.
dashboard.pinnedRowHint: Cards pinned here always stay on your dashboard.
dashboard.emptyDashboardHint: No cards selected. Use Add Card to choose what to show.
dashboard.saveConfirmTitle: Are you sure you want to save the dashboard changes?
dashboard.removeConfirmBody: Remove {card} from your dashboard? You can add it back later.

list.title: Personnel
list.profileChangeHint: Approving applies the change to the employee’s statutory profile (bank / PCB). You cannot approve your own request.
list.provisionalEndHint: Probation end for full-time (defaults to +3 months); contract or internship end otherwise. Leave blank for none.
list.orgLabelsEmptyForCompany: No organization labels are configured for the selected company.
list.emptyNoEmployeesAdmin: No employees yet — click "Create new employee" above to add one.
list.hireInitialSalaryHint: Required — effective from the join date.
list.employeeIdHint: Letters, numbers and dashes; up to 30 characters.
list.columnsHint: Tick to show. Drag to reorder.
list.columnsAbsent: Not held in Personnel yet: {fields}. Each would first have to be set up as employee information.
list.exportAria: Export the filtered employee list to Excel

incentiveDeclarations.error_invalid_period: Enter valid start and end months, with the start no later than the end.
incentiveDeclarations.error_approval_required: HR must confirm the applicable approval and eligibility before saving.
incentiveDeclarations.error_missing_reference: Enter the approval reference (up to 300 characters).
incentiveDeclarations.error_not_found: This employment or declaration is no longer available to you. Refresh and check your company access.
incentiveDeclarations.error_not_resident: Check the employee’s recorded resident tax status before saving this declaration.
incentiveDeclarations.error_citizenship_unknown: Check the recorded citizenship/PR status required for the C-Suite scheme.
incentiveDeclarations.error_overlap: This period overlaps an existing declaration. Review or revoke it before recording a replacement.
incentiveDeclarations.error_missing_declaration: No applicable approval is recorded for this employment, employer and payroll period. Complete the approval reference, effective period and HR eligibility confirmation.
incentiveDeclarations.error_stale_context: The employment’s employer changed. Refresh and confirm the approval for the current employer.
incentiveDeclarations.title: Payroll incentive declarations
incentiveDeclarations.hint: HR records existing approval for this employer and period. Eligibility is not determined automatically.
incentiveDeclarations.eligibilityConfirmed: HR confirms the applicable scheme conditions, including approved company, resident and non-citizen requirements for C-Suite.
incentiveDeclarations.revokeHint: Revoke an incorrect declaration, then record a new one. Existing payroll history is preserved.
incentiveDeclarations.legacyHint: REP or Knowledge Worker on the person record does not authorize future payroll. A declaration for the current employer and period is required.
incentiveDeclarations.error_invalid: Check the employer, scheme, period, approval reference and eligibility confirmation.
incentiveDeclarations.error_unavailable: Declarations are unavailable for this employment or access scope.
incentiveDeclarations.error_saveFailed: Declaration could not be saved. Check the approval, period and employment scope.
incentiveDeclarations.error_revokeFailed: Declaration could not be revoked. Refresh and check access.
incentiveDeclarations.ready: Tax configuration is ready for this payroll period
incentiveDeclarations.error_declaration_revoked: The recorded approval for this employer and payroll period was revoked. Record the applicable approved scheme before recalculating.
incentiveDeclarations.error_declaration_outside_period: The recorded approval does not cover this payroll period. Complete the applicable approval period before recalculating.

detail.maritalPcbNote: Marital status here drives leave eligibility only. Update the PCB/tax category separately if it also changes.
detail.taxNumberSharedTitle: {count, plural, one {This income tax reference number is already filed against another employee: {names}. Correct whichever record is wrong before you file — the CP39 prints what is stored under each employee.} other {This income tax reference number is already filed against other employees: {names}. Correct whichever record is wrong before you file — the CP39 prints what is stored under each employee.}}
detail.socsoCategoryHint: Auto follows PERKESO rules from the employee's age and citizenship. Pick a specific category to override, or No contribution to exempt SOCSO.
detail.eisCategoryHint: Auto follows PERKESO rules. Choose No contribution to exempt EIS.
detail.subjectToSkbbkHint: SKBBK (Lindung 24 Jam) — the self-employment injury scheme leg added on top of SOCSO.
detail.employerBearsHint: The contribution is still made and reported in full; the employee's share is funded by the employer instead of deducted from net pay.
detail.employerBearsEpfHint: When ticked, the employee's EPF contribution is still computed and reported in full, but the employer funds it instead of deducting it from net pay.
detail.tp3SectionTitle: Previous employment this year (TP3 / opening balances)
detail.tp3SectionDescription: From the employee’s Form TP3 (or pre-migration payroll): seeds the PCB accumulators when the year matches the pay period. Never shown on payslips or the EA.
detail.zakatSummaryDescription: Read-only summary of the current zakat election. Manage it in Payroll → Transaction Entry → Zakat.
detail.zakatSummaryInactive: No active zakat election for this employee.
detail.othersStatutoryHint: Statutory settings that do not belong under EPF, SOCSO, EIS or Tax Information.
detail.subjectToHrdfHint: When checked, this employee's qualifying earnings are included in the HRD Corp (HRDF) levy calculation during payroll; when unchecked, the employee is excluded entirely.
detail.subjectToHrdfFollowingDefault: Following the company's HRDF registration default. Save to set an explicit choice for this employee.
detail.subjectToHrdfCompanyNotRegistered: Set to Yes, but this employee’s company has no HRDF Contribution Rate (Organization ▸ Statutory), so payroll charges no levy for them. The choice is saved and takes effect once the company is registered.
detail.subjectToHrdfCompanyUnregisteredNote: This company has no HRDF Contribution Rate (Organization ▸ Statutory), so choosing Yes here is saved but charges no levy until the company is registered.
detail.dataPrivacyNote: Run a retention-guarded PDPA erasure for this employee — destroys what it can, keeps what statute requires.
detail.directSuperiorSearch: Search by employee ID or name
detail.directSuperiorHint: The reporting and approval hierarchy is derived automatically by following each employee's Direct Superior — no approval levels to configure.
detail.terminateConfirmDescription: This ends {name}'s employment on the chosen date. Assignment history is preserved.
detail.epfModeManualFixed: Manual (by fixed amount) — RETIRED, replaced by the three Manual (by Amount) categories (item 70b14723)
detail.epfElectionHint: Voluntary excess (i-Topup, KWSP Form 17A/18A) sets a rate at or above the statutory 11%/13%; a blank side stays statutory. The Manual (by Amount) categories use an exact ringgit figure instead of a rate, and a reason is required for them. Exempt is for legitimately-exempt employees only.
detail.payComponentsHint: Recurring pay items for this employee. Applied to payroll once typed components are enabled.
detail.dateError: Effective end date cannot be before the effective start date.
detail.amountError: Amount must be greater than zero.
detail.currencyUnsupported: Only MYR is supported — payroll is computed in MYR.
detail.epfVoluntaryHint: Enter each side's total rate at or above the statutory floor (employee 11%, employer 12–13%). Leave a side blank to keep it statutory.
detail.epfSemiAutoHint: Enter the employee rate at or above the statutory 11%. The employer side stays automatic (statutory).
detail.gradeMovementOnlyNote: The Grade can’t be changed here. Record it as a movement so it is dated, attributable and shown once on the Employment History:
detail.cp38Hint: CP38 applies by payroll month — periods are month-aligned (a mid-month instruction charges the whole month it starts in) and the amount is deducted in addition to monthly PCB.
detail.cp38ProcessedError: This pay period is already processed — the CP38 record cannot be changed for it.
detail.encashmentUnfreezeConfirmDescription: This re-opens the leave ledger so corrections (e.g. cancelling a booking) can be made. Adjust to re-lock afterwards.
detail.encashmentHint: The effective figure (override, if set, else the auto figure) is what Payroll's leavers panel uses. Adjusting re-locks the balance; a mandatory reason is recorded on both actions.

family.title: Family & Dependents Information
family.note: For benefits and insurance records only. These do not affect payroll or the tax number of children, and are separate from the emergency contact.
family.name: Name
family.hint: HR maintains these records. Employees cannot edit their own family details in this version.
family.childReliefGuidance: LHDN child relief (per child): under 18 — RM2,000; 18+ in full-time pre-university study (e.g. A-Levels, matriculation) — RM2,000; 18+ in diploma/degree study and above — RM8,000; disabled child — RM8,000; disabled child in full-time higher education — RM16,000. Claim 100% for one parent, or 50% each when parents share the claim.
family.ageHint: Guidance only: under 18 usually falls under “Child under 18”; 18 and over in full-time study usually falls under a study category. The category is never set automatically — the administrator chooses it.
family.deleteFamilyConfirmBody: This removes the family member from the family register. If child relief is on automatic mode, the employee's child-relief count is refreshed accordingly.

qualification.title: Qualification Information
qualification.deleteConfirmBody: Remove this qualification record? It will no longer appear in this employee's qualification history.
qualification.hint: HR maintains these records. Qualification types are managed under System Settings > System Labels > Profile Options.
qualification.highestHint: Only one record can be the highest qualification. Ticking this moves the marker off the previous record.

clocking.hint: When geofencing is enforced, clock-in/out is blocked unless the employee is within the radius of an assigned site. When off, location is still captured for audit.
clocking.noAssignedSites: No clocking sites are saved for this employee yet. The sites ticked above are proposed from their work location and will be assigned when you press Save. While geofencing is on, their clock-in is refused until at least one is saved.
clocking.noSharedSites: No shared clocking locations exist yet. A group administrator adds them under Attendance › Clocking location.
clocking.linkedPoints: {count, plural, =0 {No clocking point is linked to this employee’s work location yet, so nothing is pre-ticked.} one {# clocking point is linked to this employee’s work location and is pre-ticked.} other {# clocking points are linked to this employee’s work location and are pre-ticked.}} Every shared clocking location is offered in the list above, not only those.
clocking.assignmentIntro: Assign the locations where this employee is allowed to clock in and clock out.
clocking.noneAssigned: No locations assigned. This employee cannot clock in anywhere while geofencing is enforced.

employmentInfo.title: Employment Information
employmentInfo.yearOfServiceTooltip: Group Join Date: {groupJoinDate} · Service as of: {asOf}
employmentInfo.companyChangeableHint: This employee has no transactions yet, so you can still correct their Company here. Choose the correct company, then pick their Department and Save.
employmentInfo.companyPendingBanner: Moving this employee to {company}. Pick their Department and Save to confirm — nothing changes until you Save.
employmentInfo.companyLockedNote: The Company can’t be changed here because this employee already has recorded activity. Use the Movement tab to record a Transfer, which keeps their history intact.
employmentInfo.companyLockedTooltip: Locked — this employee has recorded activity. Use Movement to record a Transfer.
employmentInfo.destinationNotAdministered: You can only move this person to a company you manage. To move them to another company, use the Movement tab to record a Transfer.
employmentInfo.readOnlyNote: Company, Department, Position, Job Grade, Employment Type and Employee Status are shown for reference. Manage them under Movement (transfers) and the Profile tab (grade) to keep their history intact.
employmentInfo.superiorNote: Set the Direct Superior on the card below.
employmentInfo.employeeStatusDerivedNote: Employee Status is worked out automatically from the employment dates and shown as a read-only badge — no manual step.
employmentInfo.blacklistNote: Blacklisting is a deliberate HR action and overrides the automatic Employee Status.
employmentInfo.contractRemarkPlaceholder: e.g. Initial 12-month employment contract. Renewable upon performance review.
employmentInfo.contractNote: Shown for contract employees only. The start date defaults to the Group Join Date until you save one, and the end date is the same date the contract expiry review watches.
employmentInfo.lifecycleDeferredNote: Resignation and last working dates are captured here for records. Wiring them into payroll final pay and attendance cut-off is planned as a follow-up.
employmentInfo.assignmentViewOnlyNote: This information is view-only. Organisation assignment changes are recorded as movement events, so each one keeps its effective date, its reason and its place in the employment history.
employmentInfo.joinDatesViewOnlyNote: Both join dates are view-only. They are set together when the employee is created; afterwards a Join Date Change records a move to another company in the group, and a Group Join Date Correction records an authorised fix to the master service date.
employmentInfo.pendingMovementTitle: Scheduled changes not yet in effect
employmentInfo.pendingMovementNote: The values below are today's. They will not change until each date arrives.

documents.title: Documents
documents.intro: Central repository for this employee's supporting documents. Upload, categorize, view, download, update or remove files. Statutory identifiers are managed on the Bank & Statutory tab.
documents.supportedTypes: Supported: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JPG, PNG, TXT (max 10 MB).
documents.confirmDelete: Delete this document? This cannot be undone.
documents.replaceHint: Choose a new file to replace the current attachment

detail.zakatMoved: Zakat has moved to Payroll → Transaction Entry → Zakat.
detail.backupShiftHintFixed: The shift used on any day this employee is not rostered. On a Fixed arrangement that is every working day — roster only the days that differ.
detail.backupShiftHintRoster: The shift used on any day this employee is not rostered. Rostering stays optional: a day with no roster entry falls back to this shift.
detail.shiftTypeHint: Every employee has a backup shift — the shift used on any day they are not rostered. Fixed: they work it every working day, and the roster records only the exceptions. Roster: they are normally scheduled from the Roster screen, and the backup shift covers any day with no roster entry. A dated roster entry always wins; overtime and lateness are measured against whichever shift applies that day. Changing this does not alter attendance already recorded — it changes how days are calculated from now on. The change starts on the effective date you set; days before it keep the shift that was in force then.
detail.shiftEffectiveDateHint: The change starts on the effective date: days before it keep the shift that was in force then.
detail.shiftEffectiveBeforeStart: The effective date cannot be earlier than the employee's start date ({date}).
detail.shiftBackInsertRefused: This employee already has a shift change dated {date}. A change dated before that one cannot be added yet.
detail.shiftHistoryEmpty: No shift change has been recorded for this employee yet.
detail.salaryRevisionConfirmDescription: This adds a new salary record and keeps the full history. It becomes the active salary from the effective date.
detail.salaryAllowanceMovedHint: Allowances are managed in Pay Components under the Payroll module — not on this screen.
detail.salaryInitialEffectiveHint: The first record is effective from the join date.
detail.salaryDeleteConfirmDescription: This removes the record from the salary history and from payroll calculations. Records already used by a closed payroll run cannot be deleted. The removal is kept in the audit trail.
detail.salaryEditConfirmTitle: Save changes to this salary record?
detail.salaryEditConfirmDescription: This edits the latest salary record in place and keeps an audit log of the change.
detail.salaryNoResults: No salary records match your search.
detail.photoHint: PNG or JPG, up to 2 MB.
detail.customHolderHint: Pay this employee's salary into another person's account (for example a spouse or authorised person) when a banking restriction applies. This changes only the payee, never any pay amount.
detail.taxCategorySingle: Single/Spouse do not Claim Child Relief
detail.taxResidencyApprovedSchemeNote: Select REP, Knowledge Worker or C-Suite only when the employee has the required approval for this employment and year. C-Suite requires a resident non-citizen in an approved company. Eligibility is confirmed by HR.
detail.childReliefAutoSyncNote: Worked out from the Family records: {count} eligible child(ren). The tax record is rewritten when a family member is added, edited or removed — and only then, so a child reaching 18 does not move it by itself. Save this card to write the current figure back, or switch to Manual to set it yourself.
detail.childReliefAutoSynced: Children (PCB Relief) updated automatically to {count} from the Family records.
detail.childReliefAutoSyncedPayrollAlert: Children (PCB Relief) updated automatically to {count} from the Family records — but payroll for {period} is still open. Regenerating that run will now produce a different PCB. Please let the payroll team know.
detail.employerBearsTaxHint: When ticked, the employee's tax (PCB) is still computed and reported in full, but the employer funds it instead of deducting it from net pay. Tax-on-tax gross-up is a follow-up.
detail.icNumberHint: 12-digit MyKad number. Required for Malaysian employees, optional for others. Used to default the SOCSO/EIS and EPF numbers.
detail.icDobInvalidDate: The IC number's first six digits aren't a valid date, so the date of birth wasn't filled in. Enter it manually.
detail.passportHint: Passport number, issue date and expiry date are required for non-Malaysian employees. A Malaysian employee's passport is optional, but the three must be filled together. Issuing country and remark are optional.
detail.scheduleGroupNone: No schedule group — use the shift’s own rules
detail.scheduleGroupHint: The group decides this employee’s lateness, early-out and overtime rules. Leave it blank and those rules come from the shift they are on, exactly as before. A group only accepts the shifts listed against it.
detail.scheduleGroupEmpty: No schedule groups exist yet. Create one on the Schedule Group screen, and list the shifts it allows.
detail.recalcHistoryHelp: Automatic adjustments made to this employee’s leave entitlement after a profile change (grade, employment type, hire date or confirmation). “Took effect” is the date the change itself took effect, not the date it was recorded. Where a change took effect in an earlier leave year, the correction applies to the current one and this column shows the date it was posted.
detail.payModeBoundaryError: A pay-mode change must take effect on the first day of a month (the start of a pay period). Salary amount changes may use any date.
detail.payModeBoundaryHint: Pay Mode changes must take effect on the 1st of a month; the daily and hourly modes also need a rate. Basic salary stays the monthly-equivalent wage used for statutory calculations.
detail.salaryNoBasicHint: Basic salary may be left blank or 0 for an employee with no monthly basic — a Director paid quarterly fees, for example. Remarks is then required and must say why.
detail.salaryRemarkRequiredError: This salary record has no basic amount, so Remarks must say why — for example, paid by quarterly director's fees. Payroll will leave this employee out of any month with nothing to pay them.
detail.salaryNegativeError: Basic salary cannot be a negative amount. Leave it blank or enter 0 for an employee with no basic salary.
detail.salaryNotANumberError: Basic salary must be a number. Leave it blank or enter 0 for an employee with no basic salary.
detail.paymentMethodBankHint: Bank Transfer requires both a bank name and an account number on the Bank & Statutory tab. Without them the change is rejected, so an unpayable record never reaches the bank file.
detail.payPolicySourceNote: Pay Mode and Payment Term come from the payroll policy <link>{policy}</link> and are shown here for reference. Edit them on the policy so every employee using it stays consistent.

movement.title: Employment History

form.terminateConfirmDescription: This ends the employment on the effective date and closes the current assignment. The action is recorded in the audit trail.
form.comparisonHint: Only the fields you change are recorded. A value left as it is stays untouched and creates no history entry.
form.editHint: Saving a correction rolls this event back and records the corrected version. The original stays in Employment History, marked as corrected — it is never removed.
form.payrollWarning: A processed payroll run already covered this period. Payslips are not reprocessed automatically.
form.joinDateChangeHint: The date you enter becomes the employee’s new Join Date with their current company. Their Group Join Date does not change.
form.groupJoinDateCorrectionHint: The date you enter becomes the employee’s corrected Group Join Date. This is the date years of service is calculated from, so it can change their leave entitlement.
form.confirmationHint: The date you enter is the employee's confirmation date, and any changes on the right take effect from it. Leave the right-hand column untouched to confirm without adjusting salary or anything else.
form.terminationPayrollFlag: Termination saved. A payroll run has already been processed for {periods}, past the termination date — review that run. It was not changed.
form.entityTransferDateHint: This date is when the transfer takes effect, and it also becomes the employee’s Join Date with the company they are moving to. Their Group Join Date does not change, so their service, leave and long-service entitlement carry across.
form.entityTransferHint: Choose the company the employee is moving to. The Business Unit, Department, Position and Work Location lists below now show the destination company’s options — pick a Department there. Their employee ID, Group Join Date and history stay exactly as they are.

movement.rollbackConfirmDescription: The employee's details revert to what they were immediately before this event, and the entry comes off the profile. Nothing is erased — the audit record keeps who did it, when and why, and Show puts the entry back on the list.
movement.rollbackConfirmPayroll: A processed payroll run already covered this period. The rollback will NOT reprocess any payslip — reprocess it separately if that is what you need. The employee's details revert and the entry comes off the profile; nothing is erased, and Show puts it back on the list.
movement.cancelConfirmDescription: This event has not taken effect yet. Cancelling it means it will never apply, none of the employee's details change, and the entry comes off the profile. Nothing is erased — the audit record keeps who did it, when and why, and Show puts the entry back on the list.
movement.payrollLocked: Locked by a closed payroll run
movement.correctedHidden: {count, plural, one {# corrected entry hidden} other {# corrected entries hidden}}

hireCorrection.title: Correct hire details
hireCorrection.companyEditableNow: No activity has been recorded yet, so you can still correct it on the {tab} tab.
hireCorrection.companyLocked: Activity such as payroll has been recorded, so the Company is locked: use {type} from the date the change applies.
hireCorrection.payslipRefusal: Refused if payslips already exist between the old and the new date.
hireCorrection.notYet: Not part of this correction yet.
hireCorrection.laterNone: No later record carried these values forward. Only the Hired record changes.
hireCorrection.confirmTitle: Save correction to the Hired event?
hireCorrection.currentUnchanged: {field}: does not change — {record} set it later
hireCorrection.confirmNote: The original Hired record is kept and marked “Hire details corrected”. Issued payslips are not changed.

emergency.deleteConfirmBody: Remove this contact? The employee's other emergency contacts are unaffected.
emergency.name: Contact name
emergency.primaryHint: Only one contact can be the primary. Choosing Primary here moves the marker off the previous contact.

detail.disabledIndividualHint: A registered disabled individual is entitled to a further annual tax relief. Setting this to Yes changes the employee's monthly tax: because monthly tax is worked out from the year to date, the month you change it in absorbs the correction for the year so far.
detail.disabledSpouseHint: A registered disabled spouse entitles the employee to a further annual tax relief. This applies only when the tax category is Married & Spouse Not Working — the official rules give it no effect otherwise, so it is recorded and shown but does not change the deduction for any other category. Where it does apply, the month you change it in absorbs the correction for the year so far.
detail.childReliefTableNote: Key the number of children in each official relief category. Use the 100% column when this employee claims the whole relief for that child, and the 50% column when the claim is shared with the other parent — a child in the 50% column is worth exactly half that category’s relief. Whole numbers of zero or more only. The Children (PCB relief) figure above is the total of this table.
detail.locationSuggestionNote: Nothing is saved until you press Confirm. A work location moves payroll and overtime history, so it is never changed for you.
detail.locationBranchUnmapped: {branch} has not been given a work location yet. Map the branch to a location under Organization, Locations and it will be proposed here. This does not affect where the employee may clock in — that is set under Location assignment below.
detail.locationNoBranch: No branch is recorded on the Employment tab, so no work location can be proposed from it.
detail.payComponentOverlap: This employee already has a {code} pay component covering {from} to {to}. End that record first, or choose dates that do not overlap it.
detail.payComponentBackwards: This employee already has a {code} pay component starting {from}. A new value must take effect on or after that date.
detail.payComponentMidMonth: A change to the {code} pay component has to take effect on the first of a month. This employee already has a live {code} record covering part of that month, so a change dated part-way through it would pay both records in full. Use {nextFirst}.
detail.payComponentClosedRun: Pay run {period} is closed, so the {code} pay component can no longer be changed for that period.
detail.tp3FormNote: These four figures are what the monthly PCB reads, and they stay that way. The full TP3 — the previous employers, the gross / exempt / EPF boxes the form asks for separately, and its seventeen relief categories — is kept on its own screen, where the form can also be printed.
detail.childReliefModeAutoTableHint: Auto (from table) values each child by their official relief category instead of the flat per-child amount — a child in full-time diploma or degree study is worth far more than a child under 18. Choosing it reveals the category grid below; until that grid is keyed it claims nothing, so key it before saving. The Child relief review screen shows what the change is worth in ringgit for everyone at once.
detail.childProvenanceFromFamily: Worked out from the Family records
detail.childProvenanceFromTable: Worked out from the relief table below
detail.childFamilyCountHint: The Family records hold {count} child record(s).
detail.childReliefAmountHint: Child relief: RM {amount} — Form EA Section D item 6 prints this figure.
detail.childQualifyingManualNote: Manual mode uses the number entered above as the qualifying count, at RM {amount} per child. Switch to a derived mode to work it out from each child's own category.
detail.childQualifyingBreakdown: How the qualifying count was reached
detail.childQualifyingBreakdownEmpty: Nothing is keyed yet, so no child relief is claimed.
detail.childQualifyingBreakdownUnsupported: [retired r351 — replaced by childQualifyingBreakdownUnitemised; it opened with 'No children are recorded in the Family register' but rendered on an empty row count, so it also fired when children WERE recorded and none of them qualified]
detail.childQualifyingBreakdownUnitemised: There is nothing to itemise here, but RM {amount} of child relief is still being claimed from the stored head count above.
detail.childQualifyingAutoUnitsNote: Every eligible child is counted as one qualifying child here, because at least one of them has no relief category recorded. The weighting only applies once every qualifying child has one — add the missing category on the Family tab and this figure follows on the next payroll run.
detail.childQualifyingUncategorised: {count} eligible child(ren) carry no relief category, so they would add nothing to a figure priced by category.
detail.childQualifyingStaleFamily: [retired r351 — replaced by childQualifyingPayrollBehind; it compared head counts only, so a stale relief GRID moved the money with the counts equal and the card said nothing]
detail.childQualifyingPayrollBehind: Payroll is still deducting RM {storedAmount} of child relief ({storedCount} qualifying child(ren)) — the figure last written to the tax record. The Family records as at {date} support RM {amount} ({count}). Saving this card writes the worked-out figure back, and the next payroll run uses it.
detail.childQualifyingNoneEligible: {count} child(ren) are recorded in the Family register, and none of them counts towards child relief as at {date}. A child counts while they are under 18, or at any age while they are recorded as in full-time education. Check each child's date of birth and student status on the Family tab.
detail.childQualifyingNoDob: {count} child record(s) carry no date of birth, so their age cannot be confirmed and they are not counted: {names}. Add the date of birth on the Family tab.
detail.childQualifyingWeightingGap: The relief categories recorded against these children come to {ruleUnits} qualifying children — {ruleAmount} of relief — but only {amount} is being given, because at least one qualifying child has no category recorded and the weighting cannot be applied to a partly-filled record. This employee's monthly tax is therefore over-deducted. Adding the missing category releases the rest.
detail.childQualifyingWeightingGapOver: The relief categories recorded against these children come to {ruleUnits} qualifying children — {ruleAmount} of relief — which is LESS than the {amount} currently being given. Every child is being counted as one whole child, so a child whose claim share is recorded as 50% (the other half claimed by the other parent) is still counted in full. This employee's monthly tax is therefore under-deducted, and the shortfall is settled at the annual assessment.
detail.childQualifyingAutoWeightedNote: Each child is counted at the weight its relief category carries: a child 18+ in diploma or degree study, and a disabled child, each count as four, and a disabled child in that study as eight. This is the same figure the payslip uses.
detail.childQualifyingWhyExplicit: [retired r355 — the tick is consent, not eligibility (77e882f5); replaced by childQualifyingWhyCategory]
detail.childQualifyingCategoryContradictsDob: This child’s relief category says under 18, but their date of birth does not. Check the record.
detail.childQualifyingWhyCategory: Counted because this child’s relief category allows a claim past 18. The tick alone does not qualify a child.
detail.childrenPhysicalDoc: The number of children who qualify. Form EA item 8, Form E and CP8D read this one.
detail.childrenQualifyingDoc: LHDN’s C — a weighting, not a number of people: each child counted as the s.48 units its relief category carries. The monthly PCB calculation and its slip read this one; nothing on Form EA prints it. The relief it produces, RM{perChild} × C, is what Form EA Section D item 6 prints.
detail.epfManualAmountHint: Enter the exact monthly EPF contribution in ringgit. It is used from the very first payroll run and on every reprocess. A side left blank keeps the statutory calculation. An amount below the EPF Act schedule is accepted and recorded — the KWSP submission file will carry the true wage against your amount, and the agency is the one who checks them.
detail.epfManualDraftHint: The fixed-amount categories (Manual by Amount) are set on the employee’s Bank & Statutory card after the employee is created, because the amount itself is not collected here.
detail.childQualificationReviewSettings: Review the PCB child relief settings before processing payroll.
detail.taxSelectionEligibilityHint: Select the category applicable to this employment and employer. Selecting an incentive records HR’s decision that its approval, eligibility and period conditions are met. No separate declaration is required.
detail.taxSelectionConfirmationRequired: Confirm the applicable category in this field and save once. Older settings could not identify an unambiguous employer-specific choice.
detail.taxCategoryLegacy3: Category 3 — spouse working, divorced or widowed, or single with adopted child
detail.taxCategorySingleHint: LHDN Category 1 means Single. Married employees follow their spouse’s working status, even when no child relief is claimed.
detail.taxCategoryNoneExplanation: Tax Category was None for this payroll attempt. PCB was not calculated; other statutory calculations continue normally.

import.title: Import employees
import.description: Bulk-load employees, statutory profiles and pay from an Excel (.xlsx) file. Download the template, fill it in, upload it — nothing is created until you have seen the check.
import.noCompanies: Create a company before importing employees.
import.dropHere: Drop a file here or click to browse
import.uploadHint: Accepts CSV, XLSX or XLS. The first worksheet is read.
import.csvPlaceholder: Paste CSV with a header row — full_name,email,department,hired_on,ic_number,basic_salary,…
import.unsupportedFileType: Unsupported file type. Upload a CSV, XLSX or XLS file.
import.fileTooLarge: File is too large. Split it into smaller batches and try again.
import.fileReadError: Could not read that file. Check the format and try again.
import.resolveHint: Department / position resolve by name within the row's company. A blank Company column means {company}.
import.booleanHintPost: accept yes/no and default to yes.
import.importedCount: Imported {count, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}}
import.skippedCount: {count, plural, one {# skipped (had errors)} other {# skipped (had errors)}}
import.withErrorsCount: {count, plural, one {# with errors} other {# with errors}}
import.missingColumns: {count, plural, one {Missing required column:} other {Missing required columns:}}
import.instructionsHeading: How to fill in this template
import.instructionRequired: Required columns: {columns}. Every other column may be left blank.
import.instructionDates: Enter dates as real Excel dates, or type them as YYYY-MM-DD.
import.instructionIdentityText: The IC, phone, bank account, EPF, SOCSO and tax number columns are formatted as text so leading zeros are kept. Do not change their format to General.
import.instructionCompany: Leave the Company column blank to use the company selected on the import screen, or name a company to import employees for several companies in one file.
import.instructionReference: The Reference sheet lists every accepted value for Company, Department, Position and Cost Center. Anything else is rejected with the reason.
import.instructionSamples: Delete the two sample rows before uploading.
import.historyHint: Every import that has been run, and the rows that could not be loaded. The uploaded file itself is not kept.
import.historyEmpty: No imports yet. Once you run one, it is listed here with its result.
import.historyErrorsShown: {count, plural, one {# row could not be imported} other {# rows could not be imported}}
import.historyNoDetail: No row detail was kept for this import.
import.step2Hint: One row per employee on the first sheet, one row per family member on the Family sheet. Every column except the six required ones may be left blank.
import.step4Hint: Nothing is created until you confirm.
import.step5Hint: Check the rows above, then import. This is the point at which records are created.
import.step5Blocked: This file was refused as a whole. Correct it and upload it again — nothing can be imported until then.
import.familyRowsCount: {count, plural, one {# family member} other {# family members}}
import.dependentsImportedCount: {count, plural, one {# family member added} other {# family members added}}
import.superiorFailedCount: {count, plural, one {# employee was imported, but their direct superior could not be linked} other {# employees were imported, but their direct superior could not be linked}}
import.instructionPassport: Passport Number, Issue Date and Expiry Date must be filled in together, or all three left blank. Passport Issuing Country uses the same list as Nationality — see the Reference sheet.
import.instructionAddress: The address columns are the employee’s home address. State and Country must match a value on the Reference sheet.
import.instructionProbation: Probation End Date applies to full-time employees only. Probation and notice periods are whole numbers of months and days.
import.instructionSuperior: Direct Superior takes an Employee ID or work email. It may name someone further down this file, or someone already employed.
import.instructionSalaryRemarks: Basic Salary may be 0 — a director paid by quarterly fees, for example — but the row must then say why in {column}. Leave it blank for everyone who has a basic salary. Payroll leaves an employee with no basic salary out of any month with nothing else to pay them.
import.instructionFamily: Family members go on the Family sheet, one row each, linked to the employee by Employee ID. A CSV file cannot carry them — use this Excel file.
import.instructionFamilyWhole: If any row on the Family sheet has a problem, nothing at all is imported — not the employees either. Correct it and upload again.
import.sectionChooserHint: Each choice downloads its own template carrying only that section’s columns. Only the full template creates new employees; the four section templates update people who already exist, matched by Employee ID.
import.sectionChooserUpdateOnly: The four section templates can only update people who are already in the system — none of them adds anybody. To add a new employee, choose “Everything — new employees” and use the full template, which asks for the name, work email, department, join date and salary a new record needs.
import.sectionFullHint: The full template. One row per new employee, every detail in one file.
import.sectionProfileHint: Name, contact details, identity documents, home address and emergency contact.
import.sectionEmploymentHint: Probation and notice periods, confirmation date and direct superior.
import.sectionBankStatutoryHint: Bank account for salary payment, income tax reference, tax category and number of children.
import.sectionFamilyHint: Family members, added to employees who are already in the system.
import.sectionUpdateOnlyNotice: This template can only UPDATE people who are already in the system — it cannot add anyone. Every row is matched by Employee ID, and a row matching nobody is refused. To add new employees, go back to Step 1 and choose “Everything — new employees”. A blank cell keeps what is already recorded; it never clears it.
import.sectionStep2: Fill it in — Employee ID on every row
import.sectionStep5Hint: Check who each row lands on and what it changes, then update. This is the point at which records are changed.
import.sectionColumnsNotice: Only these columns may appear in the file. A column belonging to another section is refused, and the refusal names the section that owns it. Some columns of the full template — company, department, position, cost centre, employment type, join date, pay, and the EPF, SOCSO, EIS and tax-residency fields — belong to no section and cannot be imported per section at all; change those on the employee’s own Personnel record.
import.sectionInstructionKey: Employee ID says which person to update. It must match somebody who already exists — this template cannot create anybody. Add new people with the full employee template first.
import.sectionInstructionBlank: Leave a cell blank to keep what is already recorded. A blank never clears a value.
import.sectionInstructionOneRow: One row per employee. Two rows carrying the same Employee ID are refused.
import.sectionInstructionFamilyRow: One row per family member. The same Employee ID may appear on several rows.
import.sectionInstructionFence: This file may carry only the columns listed on this sheet. A column belonging to another section is refused and nothing is imported. Columns that belong to no section — company, department, position, cost centre, employment type, join date, pay, and the EPF, SOCSO, EIS and tax-residency fields — cannot be imported per section at all; change them on the employee’s own Personnel record.
import.sectionUpdateCount: {count, plural, one {# to update} other {# to update}}
import.sectionSkipCount: {count, plural, one {# with nothing to change} other {# with nothing to change}}
import.sectionNotFoundCount: {count, plural, one {# not found} other {# not found}}
import.sectionNotFoundNotice: {count, plural, one {# row names an Employee ID that is not in the system.} other {# rows name an Employee ID that is not in the system.}} A section file can only update people who already exist — it cannot add anyone, because it carries none of the name, work email, department, join date and salary a new employee record needs. Add those people with the “Everything — new employees” template first, then run this file again.
import.sectionUpdatedCount: {count, plural, one {# employee updated} other {# employees updated}}

fields.basicSalaryBlankPlaceholder: Leave blank if there is no basic salary
fields.remarksNoBasicPlaceholder: e.g. paid by quarterly director's fees

wizard.orgLabelsEmptyForCompany: No organization labels are configured for the selected company.

hints.provisionalEndOn: Probation end for full-time (defaults to +3 months); contract or internship end otherwise. Leave blank for none.
hints.contractEndDate: The contract expiry date — the last working day under this contract. It is stored as the contract end date on the Employment tab and drives the contract expiry review.
hints.employeeCode: Letters, numbers and dashes, up to 30 characters. It must not already be in use.
hints.dateOfBirth: Leave blank and it is taken from the identity number where possible.
hints.businessUnit: Narrows the department list only. It is not stored on the employee.
hints.hiredOn: The first day of employment. After creation this date changes only through a movement event.
hints.bankAccount: Give both the bank and the account number, or neither.
hints.noBasicSalary: Initial Basic Salary is blank or zero. Please complete Pay Mode, Payment Term and Remarks before activating the employee.
hints.companyFixed: It decides which Employee ID rule applies, and it cannot be changed once the record is created.

wizard.title: Create new employee
wizard.description: The record and its Employee ID already exist. Fill in the rest and press Activate — progress is saved at any point.

employeeId.heading: Employee ID
employeeId.chooseCompanyFirst: Choose the company above first — it decides which Employee ID rule applies.
employeeId.noSetup: No Employee ID Auto Running Number Setup is configured for the selected company. Please enter the Employee ID manually.
employeeId.ruleCompany: This company has its own Employee ID Auto Running Number Setup. The next ID it would issue is {sample}.
employeeId.ruleGlobal: The group-wide Employee ID Auto Running Number Setup applies to this company. The next ID it would issue is {sample}.
employeeId.modeLabel: How should the Employee ID be assigned?
employeeId.forcedAuto: This company's setup does not allow Manual Key In, so the running number is used.
employeeId.duplicate: Employee ID "{code}" already exists. Please enter another Employee ID.
employeeId.reserveNote: is the ID that will be issued and reserved the moment you press Create.
employeeId.heldFromCreate: The Employee ID is reserved as soon as the record is created, and cannot be given to anyone else.

wizard.createDescription: Four details and the record exists, with its Employee ID reserved. The rest can be filled in later.
wizard.createDraftNote: Creates the record as a Draft and reserves the Employee ID immediately.
wizard.companyFixedAfterCreate: The company cannot be changed — it decided which numbering rule the reserved Employee ID came from. Discard and start again if it is wrong.
wizard.discardReleasesTip: Discarding returns the Employee ID only when it was the most recent one issued. Otherwise the number stays used and the sequence skips it.

created.heading: Employee created
created.body: The record exists as a Draft. The Employee ID below is the one that was issued and is now held for this employee.

duplicates.title: Possible duplicate employee records
duplicates.description: Employees who appear more than once as separate person records. Nothing on this page changes a record.
duplicates.howToReadSuggestion: This is a suggestion, not a conclusion. Records are listed because they share a name and a joining date — two different people can do that, and a record typed with a spelling mistake will not appear here at all.
duplicates.howToReadMultiEmployment: Rows sharing a Record letter are one person holding more than one job. That is normal and is not a duplicate.
duplicates.howToReadNothingChanged: Nothing has been changed and nothing can be changed from here. Nobody will be merged or removed until you say which of these are the same person.
duplicates.activeOnlyNote: Only employees who are currently employed are checked. Records of people who have left are not listed.
duplicates.sharedDifferentDates: {n} further name(s) are shared by more than one person record but with different joining dates. Sharing a name is common, so they are not listed here.
duplicates.noneFound: No employee shares a name and a joining date with a separate person record. {n} active employees were checked.
duplicates.mayBeDifferentPeople: These may be different people — the records disagree on: {fields}
duplicates.hasBeenPaid: At least one of these records has been paid
duplicates.evidenceTitle: What these records agree and disagree on
duplicates.icPointsAtOnePerson: The IC numbers point at one person
duplicates.icNotComparable: Only {n} IC number recorded — nothing to compare
duplicates.icStatutoryNote: These IC numbers carry the same date of birth and differ only at the end — the shape of an IC number edited to get past the rule that stops two employees sharing one. EPF, SOCSO and LHDN all file against this number, so at least one of these records is being reported under an IC that is not that person's. Nothing is changed from this screen.

notCounted.assigned_by_employer: given by the employer, not by the person
notCounted.cosmetic_only: differs only in capitals or spacing

icVerdict.same_birth_date: Same date of birth ({inIc}) in both IC numbers, and it agrees with the recorded date of birth
icVerdict.same_birth_date_unverified: Same date of birth ({inIc}) in both IC numbers; no date of birth is recorded to check it against
icVerdict.birth_date_contradicts_profile: The IC numbers both give {inIc}, but the records say {onProfile}
icVerdict.different_birth_dates: The IC numbers give DIFFERENT dates of birth ({inIc})

childRelief.title: Child relief review (PCB)
childRelief.description: Every current employee with children, what their monthly tax deducts for them today, and what it would deduct on the official LHDN category table.
childRelief.howToReadToday: Relief today is what the tax calculation already deducts for this person’s children — the number of children multiplied by the flat per-child amount, unless they are already on the category table.
childRelief.howToReadSwitch: On the category table is what it would deduct if their setting were changed right now, using the category grid stored on their own record. Nobody has one unless somebody keyed it, and an empty grid is worth nothing — so the change column can be negative, which means more tax, not less.
childRelief.howToReadFamily: From the Family register is what that grid would come to if it were filled in from the relief categories already recorded against each child. It is a suggestion drawn from your own records; it is not stored anywhere and no calculation reads it.
childRelief.howToReadNothingChanges: Nothing on this page changes anybody. It has no Apply button on purpose: moving people onto the category table changes their monthly tax, so the decision is made here and carried out one record at a time.
childRelief.activeOnlyNote: Current employees only. The totals cover the companies you are allowed to see.
childRelief.amountsTitle: The amounts these figures were priced with
childRelief.amountsPendingSignOff: These category amounts come from a reputable published summary rather than the official document, because the official page is offline. They are the numbers the calculation actually applies. Check each one against the current official publication before any payroll run relies on it.
childRelief.gridEmptyWarning: No categories keyed — switching now would claim nothing for their children and raise their tax.
childRelief.familyPartial: Covers {done} of {total} children; the rest have no category recorded.
childRelief.emptyTitle: No current employee has children recorded for tax relief.
childRelief.emptyBody: This list covers current employees whose tax record carries a number of children, or who already use the category table. Record a child count on an employee’s Bank & Statutory tab and they appear here.
childRelief.shareNote: A child with no claim share recorded is counted at the full 100% claim, which is the default; a child recorded at 50% is worth half that category’s amount.
childRelief.disagreeTitle: Typed child counts above the Family record
childRelief.disagreeDescription: These employees have a child count entered by hand on their tax record that is higher than the children on file for them. Nothing here has been changed and nothing on this page changes it.
childRelief.disagreeStatChildren: Children the records do not account for
childRelief.disagreeHeadCountNote: Both counts are a plain number of children, one per child. The entered figure is the head count that Form E, CP8D and the EA statement read, and the column beside it counts the children on file the same way. The official relief categories, which count some children as four or eight, are a separate question and are not used in either column.
childRelief.disagreeNotAnErrorNote: An entered figure is not a mistake. There are good reasons to enter one, and an employee may genuinely have children who were never added to the Family record — in which case the figure is right and the record is what is incomplete. This list only says the two disagree; it does not say which one is wrong.
childRelief.disagreeNoBulkNote: There is deliberately no way to change these in one go. Correcting a figure raises that employee’s tax from the next payroll run, and it does not touch payslips already issued, so each one is a decision to make on its own record with the reasons in front of you.
childRelief.disagreeAutoCaveatNote: Auto (from Family records) is the durable answer for anyone whose Family record is complete, because the figure then follows the record. Be aware that today it counts every child as one, so it is right for a child under 18 or in pre-university study and still under-claims for a child in diploma or degree study and for a disabled child.
childRelief.disagreeColRecordRM: Relief the children on file support (RM)
childRelief.disagreeCategorised: {done} of {total} have a relief category recorded.
childRelief.gapTitle: Children with no tax relief category
childRelief.gapDescription: These employees are set to work their child relief out automatically, but at least one of their qualifying children has no tax relief category recorded. Until every qualifying child has one, the relief stays on the plain head count and a child who would count for more is counted as one.
childRelief.gapWhyNote: The weighting only applies once every qualifying child has a category, because a partly-filled record would relieve fewer children than the employee actually has.
childRelief.gapNotAnErrorNote: A missing category is not a mistake on the record — it is information the employer may simply never have been given.
childRelief.gapNoBulkNote: There is no bulk fill, and there should not be: a child’s category is a fact about that child, and it can only be set on their own record.
childRelief.gapManualNote: Employees on a typed figure are not listed here. For them the typed number decides, so a category would change nothing.

leave.inquiryMovedToTracker: Employee Details, Employee Balances and Employee Leave Record now open from Team Leave Tracker; this page shows your own leave only.
leave.title: Leave
leave.description: Check your balance, apply for leave, and track your requests.
leave.balancesToggle: Show or hide the leave balance details
leave.balanceCellTitle: {taken, plural, one {# used} other {# used}} · {pending, plural, one {# pending approval} other {# pending approval}}
leave.durationLine: Duration: {cat, select, one {{v} day} other {{v} days}}
leave.cancelDatesHint: Tick the day(s) you want to give back. Only the days that can still be cancelled are listed.
leave.cancelRequestedToast: Cancellation request submitted — waiting for approval.
leave.cancelReasonNothingLeft: No dates left to cancel on this leave.

emergency.formHint: Emergency Leave uses your Annual Leave first; any remainder is taken as Unpaid Leave.
emergency.reasonCategoryHint: Choose “Illness” to use your paid Sick Leave balance first before annual/unpaid.
emergency.splitNotice: Paid balances are used first. Any remaining days are taken as Unpaid Leave (no-work-no-pay).
emergency.unpaidConsentLabel: I acknowledge that any uncovered days will be taken as unpaid leave.

maternity.allowanceNotice: Maternity leave is always 98 days. The paid maternity allowance depends on EA s.37 — supply the details below so eligibility can be confirmed.
maternity.allowanceHint: The allowance is withheld (leave granted unpaid) if qualifying service is not met or for a 5th surviving child. Leave these blank to default to paid (subject to HR confirmation).
maternity.allowanceWithheld: Paid allowance withheld — {reason}; leave granted unpaid.

errors.documentRequiredAfter: A supporting document is required for {typeName} exceeding {days} days.
errors.documentRequired: A supporting document is required for {typeName} (e.g. a medical certificate).
errors.employeeRemarkRequired: An employee remark is required for {typeName}.
errors.backdatingNotAllowed: {typeName} cannot be backdated more than {days} day(s).
errors.unpaidConsentRequired: This emergency leave would take {days} day(s) as unpaid leave. Please tick the box to acknowledge the unpaid days.

summaryTip.eligible: What you receive for the whole leave year, before anything is earned, carried, adjusted or used.
summaryTip.ytdEntitled: What you have been granted so far, up to the As at date. Leave earned month by month builds up over the year; leave granted in full up front shows the whole amount from day one.
summaryTip.broughtForward: Unused days carried into this leave year from last year.
summaryTip.adjustments: Extra or deducted days entered by HR, and automatic corrections such as reversing a grant made in error. An automatic recalculation of the entitlement itself is counted in Earned to Date, not here.
summaryTip.total: Granted so far, plus brought forward, plus adjustments — before anything you have used or applied for.
summaryTip.taken: Leave you have already used (approved and taken).
summaryTip.pendingApproval: Leave you've applied for that is still awaiting approval.
summaryTip.broughtForwardForfeited: Days carried in from last year that you lost, because they passed their expiry date or exceeded the carry limit.

breakdown.statusNotGeneratedBody: An entitlement table applies to this leave type for this leave year. The entitlement has not been generated yet, so the figures below are not the amount you are entitled to. Running Generate Entitlement grants it. If the figures do not change afterwards, this balance may be frozen for an encashment, or the country pack for this company may not be active.
breakdown.statusEarnedAccrualTitle: Earned through the year, nothing accrued yet
breakdown.statusEarnedAccrualBody: This leave type is earned gradually through the leave year. Days are added as they are earned, by Generate Entitlement or by each accrual run, and nothing has been posted for this leave year yet.
breakdown.statusEarnedMethodNotAnnualLeaveTitle: Set to an earning method only Annual Leave can use
breakdown.statusEarnedMethodNotAnnualLeaveBody: {typeName} is set to an earning method that only Annual Leave can use, so no days will be added to it until HR changes its earning method on the leave type’s Earning Method step. Any days already in this balance stay as they are.
breakdown.statusZeroEntitlementBody: An entitlement table applies to this leave type, but it grants 0 days for this length of service. Generating entitlement will not change the figures below until the table's service bands are changed.
breakdown.statusEarningMethodMissingBody: An entitlement table applies to this leave type, but no earning method has been chosen for it, so generating entitlement will grant 0.00 days until one is set.
breakdown.pooledOwnEntitlement: This leave type has no entitlement of its own: its Entitlement and Earned to Date are 0.00, and every day taken on it is deducted from the {pool} pool. Every figure below is {pool}’s own.
breakdown.statusNoEntitlementTableTitle: No entitlement table for this leave type
breakdown.statusNoEntitlementTableBody: No entitlement table has been set up for this leave type, so there is no number of days for anybody to be granted and the figures below are 0.00. An administrator creates one on the Entitlement tables screen.
breakdown.statusNoEligibilityMatchBody: No entitlement table reaches you for {typeName}, so no days have been granted and the figures below are 0.00. Nobody is listed in a benefit scheme by name: a scheme is a description — a job grade, a department, a length of service — and it is optional, needed only to choose between several entitlement tables. Ask HR to add a scheme whose description covers you, or to set a default entitlement table for this leave type.
breakdown.statusCappedByMaxBalanceBody: An entitlement table applies and grants days, but its Maximum Balance is 0, so every granted day is clamped away as soon as it is granted. An administrator sets a Maximum Balance that is at least the number of days granted.
breakdown.eligibilityRulesTitle: The benefit schemes for this leave type
breakdown.eligibilityNoRules: This leave type has no benefit schemes, and it does not need one. A scheme is optional: it is a description — a job grade, a department, a length of service — that chooses between several entitlement tables. With one table, or with a default table named, the leave type reaches everybody without a scheme.
breakdown.eligibilityNotActive: You were not employed on {date}, so no scheme can cover you on that date.
breakdown.eligibilityWhyCombination: Your details pass each condition separately, but not all of them on the same assignment record.
breakdown.eligibilityUndatedNote: Grade, gender, nationality, religion and race are not dated in this system, so they are read at today’s value however far back the date above reaches.

leaveBalanceTable.statusEarnedMethodNotAnnualLeave: Earning method for Annual Leave only
leaveBalanceTable.statusNotGeneratedTip: An entitlement table applies to this leave type for this leave year, but the entitlement has not been generated yet. Run Generate Entitlement to grant it. If the figure does not change afterwards, this balance may be frozen for an encashment, or the country pack for this company may not be active.
leaveBalanceTable.statusEarnedAccrualTip: This leave type is earned gradually through the leave year. Days are added as they are earned, by Generate Entitlement or by each accrual run, and nothing has been posted for this leave year yet.
leaveBalanceTable.statusEarnedMethodNotAnnualLeaveTip: This leave type is set to an earning method that only Annual Leave can use, so no days will be added to it until HR changes its earning method on the leave type’s Earning Method step. Neither Generate Entitlement nor Run Earned Accrual grants it in the meantime. Any days already in the balance stay as they are.
leaveBalanceTable.statusZeroEntitlementTip: An entitlement table applies to this leave type, but it grants 0 days for this length of service. Generating entitlement will not change the figure until the table's service bands are changed.
leaveBalanceTable.statusEarningMethodMissingTip: An entitlement table applies, but this leave type has no earning method chosen, so it grants 0.00 days until one is set.
leaveBalanceTable.statusNoEntitlementTableTip: This leave type has no entitlement table set up, so there is no number of days for anybody to be granted. An administrator creates one on the Entitlement tables screen.
leaveBalanceTable.statusPooledEntitlement: No entitlement of its own — draws on the {pool} pool
leaveBalanceTable.statusPooledEntitlementTip: This leave type has no entitlement table because it does not need one: every day taken on it is deducted from the {pool} pool. Giving it a table of its own is what would stop it drawing on {pool}.
leaveBalanceTable.statusNoEligibilityMatchTip: No benefit scheme describes this employee for this leave type, and the leave type has no default entitlement table, so no table decides their days. A scheme is optional and holds no list of names: it describes a population by job grade, department or length of service, it chooses between a leave type’s tables, and it is not what decides whether somebody is entitled.
leaveBalanceTable.statusCappedByMaxBalanceTip: An entitlement table applies and grants days, but its Maximum Balance is 0, so every granted day is clamped away immediately. Set a Maximum Balance that is at least the number of days granted.
leaveBalanceTable.shareBadgeTip: {cat, select, one {{v} day} other {{v} days}} of approved {type}, drawn from the {pool} pool.
leaveBalanceTable.pendingShareBadgeTip: {cat, select, one {{v} day} other {{v} days}} of {type} awaiting approval, drawn from the {pool} pool.
