multiCycleWorksheet.title: Multi-Cycle Statutory Worksheet
multiCycleWorksheet.subtitle: What EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB would be if a month with more than one payroll run were treated as one statutory month — measured on your own payroll history.
multiCycleWorksheet.readOnlyBanner: This screen only reads. It does not recalculate any payslip, change any figure that has been paid, or switch anything on. It exists to be reviewed before that decision is taken.
multiCycleWorksheet.noPackForCountry: The active company's country ({country}) has no statutory pack defining a monthly contribution unit, so there is nothing to reconcile here.
multiCycleWorksheet.yearHint: Leave blank to cover every year on file.
multiCycleWorksheet.headline: {changed} of {compared} employee-months would change, across {periods} company-months that had more than one payroll run.
multiCycleWorksheet.verdictBreakdown: Already computed as one month: {aggregated}. Both readings agree: {agree}. EPF amount set by hand: {manualEpf}. Matched neither reading: {unexplained}.
multiCycleWorksheet.totalsHint: “Paid” is the sum of the figures stored on the payslips. “Each run alone” recomputes every run from the bottom of the bands. “Month as one” treats the month as a single statutory computation. “Movement” is what would change, counted only for the employee-months whose paid figures match “each run alone”.
multiCycleWorksheet.rowsHint: How far each statutory item would move (month as one, less what was paid). Months that would change are listed first.
multiCycleWorksheet.noRows: No employee-month with more than one payroll run could be compared.
multiCycleWorksheet.truncated: Only the first 200 rows are listed. The totals above cover every row.
multiCycleWorksheet.skipsHint: Excluded months are out of scope by decision — reversals are set aside, and treating a negative as zero would understate the difference. Flagged months are ones whose inputs cannot be reconstructed from what was recorded; they are reported rather than guessed at.
multiCycleWorksheet.noSkips: Every employee-month with more than one run could be compared.
multiCycleWorksheet.exampleTitle: The working, one employee at a time
multiCycleWorksheet.exampleHint: Follow the arithmetic before reading the totals. The example below is computed from the statutory tables in force, not written down.
multiCycleWorksheet.exampleNoRow: No employee-month could be compared, so only the illustration above is shown.
multiCycleWorksheet.illustrationTitle: Illustration: salary {normal} and a second run of {second} in the same month
multiCycleWorksheet.illustrationStep1: The salary run on its own: EPF on {wage} is {epf} (employee share).
multiCycleWorksheet.illustrationStep2: The second run on its own, entering the table from the bottom: EPF on {wage} is {epf}.
multiCycleWorksheet.illustrationStep4: Taken as one statutory month — {normal} of normal pay with {second} of additional pay — the month contributes {epf}.
multiCycleWorksheet.illustrationStep5: The difference is {diff}, for one employee in one month.
multiCycleWorksheet.signOffBody: A qualified payroll officer or accountant reviews this worksheet before the month-as-one treatment is switched on. Nothing on this screen enables it; enabling stays a separate, deliberate step taken after the review.
multiCycleWorksheet.signOffAdr: Print or export this page for the reviewer's file.

controlTower.title: Payroll Control Tower
controlTower.description: Every open run, what needs a person, and whether the checks are earning their keep.
controlTower.ratioTitle: How many people does it take to run this payroll?
controlTower.ratioUnavailable: We are not showing a staffing figure yet, because it would not mean anything.
controlTower.ratioWhyNotGuessed: A headcount projection gets acted on. We would rather show you nothing than a number built on checks nobody has audited yet.
controlTower.blocked_no_verdicts: No run has been checked yet, so there is nothing to measure.
controlTower.blocked_thresholds_untuned: The sensitivity of the checks is still on the shipped starting values. Until they are tuned to your payroll, the clear rate measures the settings rather than your data.
controlTower.blocked_no_human_signal: Nobody has worked through the flagged cases yet. Until someone agrees or disagrees with them, we cannot tell you how often the checks are right.
controlTower.impliedOperators: people needed, at this exception rate
controlTower.ratioAssumption: Assumes one person can clear about {n} exceptions per cycle. That is an assumption from the design, not something measured on your data.
controlTower.mCoverageHint: Read this first. A high clear rate on low coverage is a thin result, not a good one.
controlTower.mFalsePositiveHint: How often a flagged case turned out to be fine.
controlTower.mNoSignal: Needs someone to work the queue first.
controlTower.mMttrHint: Median time from flag to decision.
controlTower.metricsBasis: Based on {verdicts} checked employees across {runs} open run(s); {resolved} flagged case(s) resolved.
controlTower.thresholdsUntuned: Sensitivity is still on the shipped starting values — tune it against a real month before quoting these figures to anyone.
controlTower.noRuns: No processed runs. The tower has nothing to watch until a run is processed.

agents.title: AI agents
agents.description: The parts of this system that act on their own, and whether each of them actually can.
agents.heading: What runs without being asked
agents.headingHelp: Each of these is off until you switch it on, and switching one on is not the same as it being able to work — a switch that has nothing behind it says so below.
agents.blockedModule: Nothing will happen: {module} is not part of your plan.
agents.blockedProvider: Nothing will happen: no AI provider is set up, so there is no model for it to ask.
agents.providerHelp: An AI provider is set up under Administration → AI. Without one, the parts of these agents that need a model do nothing and record nothing — which is correct behaviour, not a fault.
agents.readOnlyNotice: You can see the state of each agent here, but switching one on or off is a group-wide change and needs a group administrator.
agents.unknownAgent: That is not one of the agents on this screen.
agents.measuredTitle: How we will know whether it helps
agents.measuredBody: Every suggestion these agents make is recorded with what happened to it, so their accuracy becomes a measured figure rather than an opinion. Nothing has been recorded yet, because none of them has been switched on — and we would rather show you nothing than a percentage worked out from no evidence.
agents.seeHowItWorks: See how the whole loop works

agentDoes.nudge: Chases whoever can fix an incomplete employee record — the employee for their own bank details, HR for everything only HR can key in.
agentDoes.hypotheses: Looks again at the people a payroll run cleared, comparing each with their colleagues. It can only ask for a second look — it can never block a run.
agentDoes.triage: Reads each new expense claim and, if the description does not fit the rest of the claim, asks the person who filed it. It can never refuse or change a claim.

refused.not_group_admin: Only a group administrator can change this.
refused.not_tenant_scoped: That setting is not yours to change.
refused.not_customer_visible: That setting is managed by Stradaverse.
refused.wrong_type: That is not a valid value for this setting.

exceptions.title: Exceptions
exceptions.description: Every flagged employee still waiting for a decision, from every payroll run, in one list.
exceptions.capped: Showing the {shown} most urgent of {total}. Clear some and the rest appear.
exceptions.help: Most urgent first: anything blocking a run, then whatever has waited longest. Deciding one here is the same as deciding it on its own payroll run.
exceptions.emptyBody: Every flagged employee across every run has been decided.
exceptions.whyBody: Three of the figures on the Control Tower — how often the checks are wrong, how long an exception waits, and how many people this workload implies — cannot be worked out until somebody decides these. Until then the Tower shows what is missing instead of a number, on purpose.

controlTower.agreementTitle: Does the AI agree with us?
controlTower.agreementWhyNotGuessed: We show no figure rather than a flattering one. A rate needs decisions to divide by, and until there are some, any percentage here would be a claim about accuracy that nothing supports.
controlTower.agreementBlocked_no_provider: No AI provider is configured, so nothing that uses a model can run.
controlTower.agreementBlocked_no_agent_on: No unattended agent is switched on for this company.
controlTower.agreementBlocked_nothing_proposed: No proposal has been recorded yet.
controlTower.agreementBlocked_nothing_decided: Proposals exist, but nobody has approved or declined one yet — so the agreement rate has nothing to divide by.
controlTower.agreementDashMeaning: A dash means not measured yet, never zero. Adjudication pass is how often the proposal was even valid; agreement is how often a person then approved it; reversal is how often an approval was later undone.
controlTower.proposalType_pay_rule_draft: Pay rule drafted from a sentence
controlTower.proposalType_close_fixed_upstream: Close a finding whose cause is fixed
controlTower.proposalType_readiness_nudge: Nudge to complete a missing record
controlTower.proposalType_anomaly_hypothesis: Possible issue the rules did not catch
controlTower.proposalType_input_triage: Question back to whoever filed a claim
controlTower.proposalType_readiness_fix: Suggested fix for an incomplete record
controlTower.agreementClosuresPending: Reversed counts closures the system has been able to check: a closure is only tested when that employee is next paid. {n} closure(s) have not reached their next payroll yet, so they are not in this figure either way.

privacy.title: Data Privacy & Audit Integrity
privacy.subtitle: Verify the tamper-evidence of the audit log and run PDPA data-erasure requests.
privacy.chainDisabled: The tamper-evidence hash chain is not enabled. New events will chain once AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN_ENABLED is on.
privacy.chainIntact: Intact — {n} events verified, no tampering detected.
privacy.chainBroken: Chain broken from event #{seq} — the log may have been altered.
privacy.chainPartial: {n} earlier events are outside the chain — they were recorded while hash chaining was off and cannot be verified.
privacy.integrityNote: Each event is hash-linked to the previous one, so an inserted, deleted, reordered or mutated row is detectable.
privacy.erasureNote: Malaysia has no blanket erasure right — this destroys what it can and withholds anything under statutory retention (≈7 years for tax/EPF/SOCSO), reporting both.
privacy.confirmLabel: I understand this permanently destroys the selected data and cannot be undone.

systemLabels.pasteHint: Tip: paste rows straight from a spreadsheet to add them in bulk.

leave.workspaceFilterEmpty: No leave types in this view.

subStep.yearTypeCompanyDefault: Company default (follow the company leave cycle)
subStep.yearTypeHelp: Types without a choice follow their company's saved leave cycle; picking a value overrides that cycle for this type only.
subStep.earningMappingHelp: Three methods, each doing something different. None hands the entitlement over up front — for Annual Leave a mid-year joiner is still credited only the months remaining in their hire year, and Sick and Hospitalisation leave are credited in full whatever month someone joins. Monthly Accrual earns one twelfth each month, credited on the day you choose. Daily Accrual earns the annual entitlement in daily slices across the leave year, then applies the leave type's rounding rule.
subStep.earningHelp: The earning method is a leave-TYPE setting: one choice here governs every entitlement row under this type, whatever the company or grade. Changing it takes effect on the next grant, accrual run or recalculation.
subStep.roundingHelp: Applied as the final step, AFTER the entitlement calculation — the earning rule itself is unchanged. Choose No Rounding to keep the calculated value exactly, or Custom Rounding and write the table yourself. The rounded figure is the one credited, so it flows through the leave balance, YTD entitled, the entitlement breakdown and the accrual process. Set separately for each leave type.
subStep.carryNoneDormant: Carry forward is off, so nothing carries into the next leave year. The maximum of {days} day(s) set earlier is kept but dormant — it has no effect on any balance, and it will apply again if you switch carry forward back on.
subStep.carryHelp: Fixed maximum keeps up to the cap; percentage keeps that share of the balance still held at year end. The two are alternatives — with percentage, the percentage alone decides the figure. The expiry fields decide when the carried portion lapses (a date, or X months after year-end).
subStep.carryStepHelp: A front door to the active entitlement policy's carry-forward settings — the per-policy controls under Eligibility remain the underlying truth.
subStep.carryAnnualOnly: Carry-forward applies to Annual Leave — this type's balance does not roll over.
subStep.yearTypeStepHelp: Choose the leave cycle first. The Earning Method and Rounding steps that follow decide how leave is credited within that cycle.
subStep.roundingWorkedExample: With this rule, a calculated {raw} days is credited as {rounded} days.
subStep.roundingCustom: Custom rounding (fill in the table below)
subStep.roundingBandsHelp: Each row covers a range of the decimal part of a calculated entitlement, from From to To with both figures included, and turns that decimal into Round To. For example, a row of 0.25 / 0.49 / 0.50 turns 10.30 days into 10.50, and a row of 0.75 / 0.99 / 1.00 turns 10.90 into 11.00. Use at most two decimal places. Whole figures are never moved, and a decimal no row covers keeps its exact value.
subStep.roundingBandBlank: Every row needs a From, a To and a Round To.
subStep.roundingBandDecimals: Use at most two decimal places, for example 0.25.
subStep.roundingBandRange: From, To and Round To must each be between 0.00 and 1.00.
subStep.roundingBandOrder: A row's From cannot be above its To.
subStep.roundingBandOverlap: {from} to {to} overlaps {otherFrom} to {otherTo}. Two ranges cannot cover the same figure, and a range includes both its From and its To.
subStep.roundingBandDuplicate: {from} to {to} is entered twice. Remove the duplicate row.
subStep.roundingBandGap: No row covers {from} to {to}. A calculated value whose decimal lands there keeps its exact value.
subStep.earningNotConfiguredNote: This leave type is not configured. It grants nothing and earns nothing — for existing employees, for new joiners, and when anything else triggers a recalculation — until you choose an earning method and save. Saving one then credits everyone on this type the full amount owed, in one upward correction.
subStep.earningLegacyMethodNote: This leave type stores an earning method that is no longer offered. It is shown here read-only and is kept exactly as it is when you save; the calculation still honours it. Choose one of the three current methods to replace it.
subStep.accrualDayHelp: Leave is credited on this day of each month. In a month shorter than the day you pick, it is credited on that month's last day — so 31 credits on 28 February, and on 29 February in a leap year. No month is ever skipped.
subStep.dailyRoundingWarning: Daily Accrual applies your rounding rule to the running total, not to each day's slice, so a rule that rounds a decimal upward will credit a whole day from the employee's very first day. No rounding is the recommended pairing with Daily Accrual.
subStep.annualLeaveSwitchOnHelp: Earned Accrual works on this leave type. Only one active leave type can be your Annual Leave.
subStep.annualLeaveSwitchOffHelp: Switch this on if this is your Annual Leave. Earned Accrual works only on Annual Leave, and only one active leave type can be your Annual Leave.
subStep.annualLeaveSwitchByCodeHelp: This leave type is recognised as Annual Leave by its code, so Earned Accrual works on it.
subStep.annualLeaveSwitchOtherRoleHelp: This leave type is already recorded as a different kind of leave, so it cannot be your Annual Leave.
subStep.annualLeaveSwitchHeldHelp: To switch this off, first change the earning method to {none} — only Annual Leave can use {monthly} or {daily}.
subStep.earningEntitlementBasedNote: {type} is entitlement-based. Only Annual Leave can be earned through Earned Accrual.
subStep.earningStrandedNote: {type} is still set to earn its days through Earned Accrual, but Earned Accrual applies only to Annual Leave, so no run adds days to it. The setting is kept exactly as it is when you save. To fix it, change the earning method to {none} (granted up front).
subStep.entitlementRoundingHelp: Applied to the Entitlement column after proration, for an employee who joined part way through the leave year. It never affects Earned to Date, which keeps its own rounding above.

conditionStep.applicationLimitHelp: Caps the total days an employee may APPLY for of this type in one leave year, whether or not any entitlement balance exists — the rule for types such as Unpaid Leave. It is checked when the application is submitted and again when it is approved. Entitlement, accrual and the balance shown in Leave Summary are untouched. Unlimited is how every leave type behaves today.
conditionStep.maxConsecutiveHelp: Caps how long ONE application of this type may be — a different rule from the yearly maximum above. Calendar Days counts every day the application spans, including weekends and public holidays; Working Days counts only the days actually charged as leave, so a Friday-to-Monday application is 4 calendar days but 2 working days. Checked when the application is submitted and again when it is approved. Where this leave type is also in a Shared Leave Group with its own per-application maximum, the stricter of the two applies and the refusal says which. Unlimited is how every leave type behaves today.
conditionStep.applicationLimitPeriodHelp: A leave year is the same as a calendar year only when your leave year starts in January. Once per employment counts across the whole time someone has worked for you, so a rehire starts fresh.

entitlementStep.tablesHint: Tables are managed in Entitlement tables. Changes made there appear here automatically. Each table takes effect from a date, and an eligibility rule decides who it applies to.
entitlementStep.accrualHint: Processes earned entitlement for a leave year — preview the dry run first, then confirm.
entitlementStep.accrualMovedPointer: Run earned accrual has a menu row of its own

leave.codeHint: Letters, digits or underscores — stored uppercase (e.g. ANNUAL)
leave.codeReadOnlyHint: Leave codes are fixed. The code is the permanent key statutory leave rules (e.g. EA-1955 annual leave, carry-forward, encashment) match on, so it cannot be renamed.
leave.codeEditableHint: Custom leave codes can be renamed. Use uppercase letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. STUDY_LEAVE). Statutory codes stay locked.
leave.saveConfirmDescription: Save your changes to this leave type?
leave.saveDatabaseError: We could not save this change because of an unexpected system problem. Nothing has been changed. Please try again, and tell your system administrator if it keeps happening.
leave.typesHelp: Statutory minimums come from the country pack (EA 1955; bands are <2 / 2–5 / 5+ years of service) and are not configurable. Grants apply the entitlement you configure — the statutory minimum is shown as guidance and a figure below it is flagged, not overridden. Days are typed in each type's Entitlement step, where each table is effective-dated and an eligibility rule decides who receives it. Annual leave pro-rates in the hire year; sick and hospitalization grant in full.
leave.earnedAccrualHelp: Tops up earned-accrual leave types to today’s accrued balance. Idempotent — safe to run any time.
leave.earnedAnnualOnly: Earned Accrual applies only to Annual Leave ({names}). Other leave types are entitlement-based and are excluded from this process.
leave.earnedAnnualOnlyNoneActive: Earned Accrual applies only to Annual Leave, and no active leave type is marked as your Annual Leave yet, so a run has nothing to work on. Open your Annual Leave under Leave config → Entitlements → Leave types and switch on “This is our Annual Leave”.
leave.earnedPreviewEmpty: No earned-accrual entitlement to generate for this scope.
leave.earnedEmptyNotSwept: Not Annual Leave: {types}. Earned Accrual applies only to Annual Leave ({swept}); other leave types are entitlement-based, so this run had nothing to examine.
leave.earnedEmptyNotSweptNoneActive: Not Annual Leave: {types}. Earned Accrual applies only to Annual Leave, and no active leave type is marked as your Annual Leave — switch on “This is our Annual Leave” on it under Leave config → Entitlements → Leave types.
leave.earnedEmptyTypeArchived: {types} is archived, and an archived leave type is never accrued. Unarchive it under Leave Config → Leave Types if its entitlement should still build up.
leave.earnedEmptyTableNotYetInForce: The entitlement table for {type} does not take effect until {validFrom}, which is after {asOf} — the date this run is calculated at. Pick a leave year on or after {validFrom}, or change when the table starts.
leave.earnedEmptyNoTable: {types} has no entitlement table in force on {asOf}. Build one under Leave Config → Entitlements before running accrual.
leave.earnedEmptyNotEarned: {types} does not earn leave by accrual — its days are granted in full, or its accrual method has not been set — so an accrual run has nothing to post for it.
leave.earnedEmptyNoEmployment: Nobody in {scope} was on the books on {asOf}.
leave.earnedEmptyNoEmploymentAll: No employee was on the books on {asOf}.
leave.earnedEmptyNoEligibilityMatch: {types} has an entitlement table, and no eligibility rule points any employee in this scope at one. The tables exist; nothing connects them to anybody. Check the eligibility rules under Leave Config → Entitlements.
leave.earnedEmptyPackInactive: Every employee in this scope works in a country with no active leave rules: {countries}.
leave.earnedEmptyFrozen: Every balance for {types} in this scope is frozen for encashment, so nothing can be accrued onto it.
leave.earnedArchivedHint: Also worth knowing: the leave type {types} is archived. Archived types are hidden from every picker on this screen and are never accrued — unarchive under Leave Config → Leave Types.
leave.earnedNothingOutstanding: Nothing outstanding: the {days} days earned up to {date} are already on the ledger. Running again posts nothing.
leave.earnedNothingEarnedYet: Nothing has been earned yet as at {date} for this scope.
leave.gradesHelp: Seniority bands. Scope a leave policy to a grade to give that grade a different entitlement; ungraded employees use the company default.
leave.gradesToggle: Show or hide the grades list
leave.serviceBandsHelp: Optional — give different entitlements by length of service, above the flat days/year. Bands must cover every service length with no gaps: the first starts at 0, the last is left open-ended. Use "under 2 years", "2 to under 5 years", "5 years and above" phrasing when explaining to staff — e.g. to match a "2–5 years inclusive = 16 days" policy, enter from 2 to 6 (entering to 5 would move an exactly-5-year employee to the next band). The statutory minimum itself steps up after 5 completed years, but it is guidance only — a band below it is flagged, not overridden.
leave.serviceBandsEmpty: No bands — the flat days/year figure above applies to everyone.
leave.archiveGradeConfirmDescription: It will be hidden from the catalog. Employees and policies already using it keep their reference.
leave.deleteTypeConfirmDescription: This permanently removes the leave type and everything configured on it. It cannot be undone.
leave.deleteTypeCascadeRules: These approval rules will be removed with it: {names}.
leave.deleteTypeCascadeBalanceSource: {names} currently takes its leave balance from this type. Deleting it clears that setting — {names} is not deleted, but it will need a new balance source before anyone applies for it.
leave.carryExpiryInvalidDate: Enter a real calendar date (e.g. 30 April, not 31 April).
leave.carryEnabledHelp: Enable carrying unused days into the next leave year. When off, leftover days are forfeited at year-end.
leave.carryIncludeEarnedHelp: Include monthly earned balance (saved as configuration)
leave.eligibilityHelp: These rules control both who can see and who can apply for this leave type. Statutory entitlements are never blocked.
leave.eligibilityUndisclosedNote: Employees who haven't disclosed the gated attribute won't see this type — ask them to complete their profile.
leave.eligibilityMultiHint: Select one or more; leave empty to allow everyone.
leave.allowedDurationsHelp: Choose which durations employees may pick for this leave type. Full day is always available.
leave.mandatoryAfterDaysLabel: Required after more than N days
leave.hrRemarkRequiredLabel: HR remark required (enforced in a later release)
leave.documentSectionHelp: Configure whether a supporting document is required, when it becomes mandatory, and which file types and sizes are accepted.
leave.affectsPayrollDeductionHelp: Set automatically: unpaid leave types reduce pay, paid types do not. This reflects whether the type is paid and cannot be edited here.
leave.payrollImpactHelp: The leave module only flags the impact on approval; the payroll module computes the actual deduction.
leave.backdatingSectionHelp: How many days back from today an employee may apply for this leave type. Leave blank for no limit. HR admins are never blocked by this limit.
leave.perDateApprovalLabel: Allow approving or rejecting individual dates
leave.perDateApprovalHelp: Lets a manager approve some dates and reject others within one multi-day request, instead of an all-or-nothing decision. Only the approved dates are deducted from the balance.
leave.perDateApprovalMultiStepNote: Applies to new requests only, and only when this company uses a single-step approval chain. While a multi-step (manager-then-HR) chain is enabled, such requests fall back to the whole-request flow with no per-date breakdown.
leave.perDateApprovalNoteReplacement: This won't apply to replacement (time-off-in-lieu) leave — those requests always use the whole-request flow.
leave.perDateApprovalNoteCounting: This only takes effect for working-day-counted, full-day leave types. This type is counted differently, so the setting has no effect.
leave.customMessagePlaceholder: Leave blank to use the default message
leave.customMessageHelp: Shown to the employee when this leave type is blocked for backdating too far. Up to 500 characters. Leave blank to keep the standard message. Applies to this leave type only.
leave.halfDayDeductionHelp: Controls how much leave is deducted when an employee applies leave on a “Half Day” work-schedule day (set on the Shift settings page). Off: deduct 0.5 day. On: deduct 1.0 full day. Full working days are never affected.
leave.halfDayDeductionFrozenNote: Applies to new applications only — leave already submitted or approved keeps the deduction amount shown at the time it was submitted.
leave.encashmentHelp: When an employee's resignation is approved, their unused Annual Leave balance can be frozen and converted into an encashable-days figure for Payroll. This module only calculates and freezes leave days — Payroll handles the ringgit conversion separately.
leave.encashmentRoundingFixed: Rounding: less than 0.5 day rounds down to 0; 0.5 day or more rounds up to the next whole day. The figure never goes below 0.

import.title: Import leave data
import.description: Upload a CSV or Excel file of leave BALANCE movements (opening balances, carry-forward, ad-hoc credits) — or paste them — preview each row, then import only the valid ones. Past leave RECORDS are loaded on Leave History Data Import instead.
import.columnHint: transaction_type is one of accrual, debit or adjustment. A debit uses negative days. TOIL (in-lieu) import is not supported here.
import.notAuthorizedError: Not authorized for this employee's company
import.toilNotSupportedError: TOIL import not supported — use the TOIL grant tool
import.uploadHint: Accepts CSV, XLSX or XLS. The first worksheet is read.
import.dropHere: Drop a file here or click to browse
import.fileReadError: Could not read that file. Check the format and try again.
import.unsupportedFileType: Unsupported file type. Upload a CSV, XLSX or XLS file.
import.fileTooLarge: File is too large. Split it into smaller batches and try again.

leave.auditHelp: Read-only history of changes to leave types, entitlements, carry-forward, approval workflow, and payroll integration.
leave.minAdvanceDayTypeHelp: Calendar Days counts every day, including weekends, rest days and public holidays. Working Days counts only the days the employee is scheduled to work. Existing leave types stay on Calendar Days, so nothing already saved changes.
leave.advanceNoticeSectionHelp: How many days before the start date an employee must submit this leave type. Leave blank for no requirement. HR admins are never blocked by this rule.
leave.advanceCustomMessageHelp: Shown to the employee when this leave type is submitted with too little advance notice. Up to 500 characters. Leave blank to keep the standard message. Applies to this leave type only.
leave.recalcToast: Corrected entitlement — recalculated {count} employee(s) ({delta} days total).
leave.deleteInUseTooltip: In use — cannot be deleted; archive it instead.
leave.applyNoticePlaceholder: Message shown to employees when they apply for this leave type
leave.applyNoticeHelp: When enabled, this message is shown to employees on the leave application form.
leave.typeMasterConfigHint: Edit a leave type's full configuration on the Entitlements tab.

essView.help: Choose which lines of the Leave Balance Summary employees see for this leave type in My Profile → Leave, and explain each one in the same place: tick an item and its Description and Formula Explanation fields appear beside it — employees see that text when they hover the item's info icon. Unticked items are hidden in self-service only; HR always sees everything. Explanations change wording only, never any leave figure. Wording is carried over from the first leave type you configured, so you only write it once; edit it here if this leave type needs different wording, and nothing is stored until you press Save.

dayTypeInclusion.help: Choose which day types are counted when calculating this leave's duration. All off deducts working days only; turn one on to also count that day type inside a leave span.
dayTypeInclusion.statutoryNote: Note: for statutory leave (Annual, Sick), the Employment Act 1955 (s.60E) requires rest days and public holidays within paid annual leave NOT to be counted — do not enable those here for statutory types.
dayTypeInclusion.summaryNone: Working days only (no rest days, holidays or shutdown days counted)
dayTypeInclusion.summaryAll: All calendar days counted (rest days, holidays and shutdown days included)

visual.help: Optional. The icon and colour theme appear beside this leave type on the employee My Profile → Leave tab. Purely visual — no effect on entitlement, eligibility or calculations.

leave.leaveUnitHelp: Whether this leave type is managed and applied in whole days or in hours. Labelling only — it does not change entitlement, accrual, workflow or payroll.
leave.deleteGradeConfirmDescription: This permanently removes the grade from the catalog. This cannot be undone.
leave.gradeInUseCannotDelete: This grade is used by employees or leave policies and can't be deleted. Archive it instead.

visibility.statutoryLocked: This is a statutory leave — employees must always be able to apply for it.
visibility.help: Tick to offer this leave type on the employee’s Request Leave screen — they can see it there and apply for it. Untick and it is neither offered nor available to apply for. To hide the leave type from the employee’s Leave tab as well, use Employee Tab Placement below.

placement.label: Placement
placement.help: Choose where this leave type appears on the employee’s Leave tab: a Primary card at the top, tucked into a Secondary group below, or Hidden from the employee entirely. Hidden is how you take a leave type off the employee’s Leave tab. Until you choose, each type uses a sensible default.

leave.duplicatePolicyAllow: Allow multiple leave applications on the same date
leave.duplicatePolicyRestrictSame: Restrict the same leave type only
leave.duplicatePolicyRestrictAny: Restrict any leave type on the same date
leave.duplicatePolicyHelp: Controls whether an employee can submit more than one leave application covering the same date. Default allows it; the two restrict options block a same-date double-booking at submission and edit.
leave.negativeBalanceYes: Yes — employees may apply even if the balance goes negative
leave.negativeBalanceNo: No — block applications that exceed the available balance
leave.negativeBalanceHelp: Controls whether an employee can submit or edit a leave application of this type that exceeds their available balance. 'No' blocks over-application at submission and edit (counting leave already pending); 'Yes' allows the balance to go negative.
leave.balanceSourceHelp: Choose which balance an application of this leave type is checked against and deducted from. 'Own Leave Balance' is the default. Pick another leave type and this type keeps no balance of its own: the application is validated against that type's balance and reduces it, while the leave history still shows this leave type. A leave type cannot point at itself, at a type that already deducts from another, or at one that already deducts from this one.
leave.allowUplYes: Yes — allow the application and treat the uncovered days as unpaid leave
leave.allowUplNo: No — validate the available balance as usual
leave.allowUplHelp: Controls whether an employee may apply for more days than their available balance. 'No' keeps the current behaviour. 'Yes' lets the application through as a single request: the days the balance covers are deducted from this leave type (or from its deduction source), and only the excess is treated as unpaid leave and passed to payroll.

formula.templateHint: Suggested wording, carried over from your first configured leave type. Edit it if this leave type differs — nothing is stored until you press Save.

sharedGroup.title: Shared Leave Groups
sharedGroup.help: A shared leave group lets several leave types draw on one pooled allowance — for example "Special Leave: 10 days a year shared between them, at most 3 days in any one application". A leave type can belong to only one group.
sharedGroup.createHint: Pick at least two leave types — a group needs two to share anything.
sharedGroup.deleteConfirmDescription: The leave types keep their own entitlements; they simply stop sharing one allowance. Leave already taken is not affected.
sharedGroup.errorAlreadyGrouped: {type} already belongs to the shared leave group "{group}". Remove it from that group first.
sharedGroup.errorNameTaken: A shared leave group named "{name}" already exists.
sharedGroup.placementHelp: Choose where this shared group appears on the employee’s Leave tab: as one balance card at the top, lower down with the other leave, or Hidden. This is separate from each leave type’s own placement — hiding a member type never changes the shared balance or what may be applied for. New and existing groups start Hidden.

leave.halfDayDeductionEmptyNote: Selecting no company turns the rule off everywhere: half days deduct 0.5 day again.
leave.maxNegativeBalanceHelp: How far below zero an employee may go. A figure is required when a negative balance is allowed, and it is the floor at BOTH stages: the application is refused if it would pass the limit, and so is the approval. The message says what the limit is and how far past it the request goes.
leave.negativeBalanceNeedsLimitTitle: Leave types allowing a negative balance with no limit set
leave.negativeBalanceNeedsLimitHelp: These leave types are set to allow a negative balance but have no maximum. They behave exactly as they do today — approval still refuses a balance below zero — because the new permission only takes effect once you enter a limit. Work through them: enter a figure where you meant it, or set the switch back to No.
leave.adjustmentsHelp: Add or take away leave days for a group of employees in one action. Choose the leave types, choose who it applies to, then enter the adjustment. Everything you do here is recorded as one action and can be reversed as a unit.
leave.adjustmentsReplacementNote: Replacement Leave is not adjusted here: every day of it is a credit with a date worked, an expiry date and a history. Add or reverse credits on
leave.adjustmentsDaysHelp: Half days are allowed, for example 0.5 or 2.5. Whether these days are added or taken away is the adjustment type you chose in step 1.
leave.adjustmentsReasonHelp: This appears on the employee’s leave record, so write what they would need to understand it, for example "CNY 2026 goodwill day".
leave.adjustmentsEmployeeSearchPlaceholder: Type a name or Employee ID…
leave.adjustmentsEmployeeNonePicked: No employee chosen yet. Search above to add someone, or paste references below.
leave.adjustmentsPasteAlternativeHelp: A second way in, for a list you already have: paste Employee IDs such as EMP-0008, or employee record references, separated by spaces, commas or new lines. To choose people by name, use the search above.
leave.adjustmentsPasteUnmatched: Not recognised, so these will match nobody: {list}
leave.adjustmentsMatchedUnknown: We could not work out who this covers. Check your selection and try again.
leave.adjustmentsEveryoneWarning: No criteria chosen yet. Leaving them all empty means this adjustment applies to EVERY employee. Check the wording on the confirmation before you save.
leave.adjustmentsRecentNone: No adjustments have been made yet.
leave.adjustmentsReverseConfirm: This writes an opposite entry for every record this adjustment created, returning those balances to where they were. Nothing is deleted, and it can only be done once.
leave.overrideSectionHelp: What the system should do when one of the rules above is not met. Choose an action per situation, then switch it on. Nothing changes for this leave type until a rule is switched on. Employees are always told what will happen and must confirm before their application is submitted.

overrideTrigger.advance_notice_not_met: When the minimum advance notice is not met
overrideTrigger.insufficient_balance: When the balance does not cover the application

overrideAction.convert_to_emergency: Offer to submit it as Emergency Leave
overrideAction.split_unpaid: Offer to take the shortfall as unpaid leave

leave.generateHelp: Generate a leave year’s entitlement in five steps: choose the leave types and the year, review how the run behaves, choose who it applies to, read the validation, then process. Nothing is written until you press Generate on the last step.
leave.generateToast: Leave year {year}: {granted} entitlement record(s) granted (one per employee per leave type), {skipped} already granted, {forfeits} forfeit(s) posted.
leave.generateToastAccrualAdded: Earned Annual Leave added for {posted} employee(s), {days} day(s) in total; {upToDate} employee(s) already up to date.
leave.generateToastAccrualNothing: Earned Annual Leave: nothing was added — Earned Accrual found no earned entitlement for these employees as at {date}.
leave.generateToastAccrualFuture: Earned Annual Leave for {year} is not added in advance — it is added as the year goes by.
leave.generateToastAccrualNotAnnualLeave: {count} earned leave record(s) are on a leave type that is not switched on as Annual Leave, so no earned days were added for them.
leave.generateToastAccrualHeldBack: {count} employee(s) were not topped up for {year}: {nextYear} has already started for them, and adding {year}'s days now would get round the carry-forward limit.
leave.generateToastAccrualFailed: The entitlement for {year} was generated and is kept, but earned Annual Leave was NOT added. Add it from Run Earned Accrual. Reason: {reason}
leave.generateGrantNone: No entitlement will be granted for this selection.
leave.generateAccrualAsAt: Earned to {date}. Earned Annual Leave is no longer counted as Failed when the earned days are added.
leave.generateAccrualFuture: {year} has not started, so earned Annual Leave is not added in advance — it is added as the year goes by.
leave.generateAccrualFailed: Earned Annual Leave could not be worked out ({reason}). Generate still grants the entitlement; the earned days can then be added from <link>Run Earned Accrual</link>.
leave.generateAccrualNothing: Nothing to add: Earned Accrual found no earned entitlement for these employees as at {date}.
leave.generateAccrualNotAnnualLeave: {count} earned leave record(s) are on a leave type that is not switched on as Annual Leave, so no earned days will be added for them.
leave.generateAccrualHeldBack: {count} employee(s) will not be topped up for {year}: {nextYear} has already started for them, and adding {year}'s days now would get round the carry-forward limit.
leave.generateIssuesAria: Employees and leave types to check

adjustmentsCriteria.asAtNote: Every criterion here is judged as at the effective date you set in step 3 — not today. Years of service and confirmation status are worked out from the hire and confirmation dates on that date.
adjustmentsCriteria.absentNote: Job Title, Employee Group and Employee Class are not held on the employee record anywhere yet, so they cannot narrow this list. Adding them is its own request.

leave.adjustmentsReviewRecords: {records, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} — {types, plural, one {# leave type} other {# leave types}} × {employees, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}}
leave.adjustmentsReviewNothing: Nothing to review yet. Go back and choose at least one leave type and at least one employee.
leave.adjustmentsIssuesNone: Nothing to flag — every selected employee can take this adjustment.
leave.adjustmentsIssueNotFound: {count} employee references were not recognised and will be ignored.
leave.adjustmentsIssueInactive: {count} employees were not employed on the effective date. They will still be adjusted.
leave.adjustmentsIssueNotEligible: {count} employees do not qualify for {leaveType} on the effective date.
leave.adjustmentsIssueFrozen: {count} {leaveType} balances are frozen for encashment and will be skipped.
leave.adjustmentsRemarksNote: There is no separate remarks field. The reason above is what the employee sees on their leave record, so write it there.
leave.generateAllTypesNote: Choosing no leave type is a real choice, not an unfinished form: the run then generates every leave type that has entitlement configured, which is what the old Generate button always did.
leave.generateSettingsIntro: These three settings were requested. Here is exactly what this release does about each of them, so nothing on this screen implies a control that is not there yet.
leave.generateSettingProrateNote: Already automatic, and not a decision this run makes. Anyone who joins during the year earns from their join date, on the earning method you configured — whether that was granted at hire or by this run.
leave.generateSettingUntilMonth: Generate leave until a chosen month
leave.generateSettingUntilMonthNote: Not in this release. Capping a year at a month changes how entitlement is calculated, and the joining grant, the monthly accrual and the automatic recalculation all have to learn the same new rule in the same change — otherwise the next profile edit quietly takes the difference back.
leave.generateSettingRecalcNote: Not in this release. It re-does a closed year’s entitlement, its brought-forward balance, its expiry and its forfeits, which moves figures employees have already seen. It arrives with its own preview of exactly what would change and its own separate confirmation.
leave.generateAsAtNote: Every criterion below is judged as at 1 January of the year you chose — not as at today. Someone who has since transferred is selected by where they were then, which is what makes a run reproducible.
leave.generateEveryoneWarning: No criteria chosen yet. Leaving them all empty means this run applies to EVERY employee. Check the matched count below before continuing.
leave.generateMatched: {count, plural, one {# employee selected} other {# employees selected}}
leave.generateEmployeeSearchPlaceholder: Type a name or Employee ID…
leave.generateEmployeeNonePicked: No employee chosen yet. Search above to add someone, or paste references below.
leave.generatePasteAlternativeHelp: A second way in, for a list you already have: paste Employee IDs such as EMP-0008, or employee record references, separated by spaces, commas or new lines. To choose people by name, use the search above.
leave.generatePasteUnmatched: Not recognised, so these will match nobody: {list}
leave.generateMatchedUnknown: We could not work out who this covers. Check your selection and try again.
leave.generateValidationHelp: This is a rehearsal of the real run, not a separate checklist: it runs the same calculation and writes nothing. What it says here is what will happen.
leave.generateIssuesNone: Nothing to flag — every selected employee will be granted entitlement.
leave.generateOutcome_unconfigured_method: No earning method chosen for this leave type, so no days can be granted
leave.generateOutcome_already_open: Already granted for this year — it will not be granted twice
leave.generateOutcome_frozen: Balance frozen for encashment, so it will be left alone
leave.generateOutcome_earned_method: Earned monthly, so it accrues through the year instead of being granted now
leave.generateOutcomeEarnedMethodNotAnnualLeav: Set to an earning method only Annual Leave can use, so no days will be added until its earning method is changed on the leave type’s Earning Method step
leave.generateOutcome_no_entitlement: No entitlement configured for this employee and leave type
leave.generateOutcome_pack_blocked: This employee’s company has no active country rules, so nothing can be calculated
leave.generateDecidedByTitle: Which entitlement rule decided each employee
leave.generateDecidedByNote: From the new entitlement rules. These do not decide anybody’s days yet — they are shown so you can check them before they take over.
leave.generateDecidedBySoleLine: {template} — the only entitlement table for this leave type, so no rule was needed
leave.generateReviewTypeCount: {count, plural, one {# leave type} other {# leave types}}
leave.generateProcessNote: Pressing Generate writes the entitlement. Running it again later is safe — anyone already granted for this year is skipped rather than granted twice.
leave.generateNothingToProcess: Nothing to process yet. Go back and choose a year and at least one employee.
leave.generateRunsNone: No entitlement has been generated yet.
leave.generateRunsLine: {selected} selected · {passed} passed · {failed} failed · {granted} records granted · {forfeits} forfeit(s)
leave.cancelApprovedSectionHelp: Whether employees may ask to cancel leave of this type after it has been approved.
leave.cancelApprovedAllowLabel: Allow employees to cancel this approved leave
leave.cancelApprovedOffNote: Employees see no cancel option for approved leave of this type. HR can still cancel on their behalf.
leave.cancelApprovedNoticeHelp: Counted for each leave day being cancelled. 0 means any day that has not started yet.
leave.cancelApprovedApprovalHelp: Re-approval goes through the same approval levels, in the same order, as the original leave request. Approved automatically cancels the leave and returns the days straight away.
leave.cancelApprovedReplacementNote: Replacement Leave cancellations always need the approver's re-approval, because giving the leave back returns its credit.
leave.cancelApprovedNotifyLabel: Notify the approver and HR when a cancellation is requested
leave.cancelApprovedNotifyHelp: Notifications appear in the notification bell. The system does not send email.
leave.generateOutcome_not_eligible: Not eligible — the leave type’s conditions exclude this employee

holidays.pageDescription: Holidays used by leave and attendance working-day counting
holidays.addHint: Holidays are matched by country and date. A day marked here is excluded from working-day leave counts and classifies attendance as a public holiday.
holidays.deleteGroupInUse: This holiday group is still assigned to employees. Reassign them before deleting it.
holidays.groupEmpty: No holiday groups yet. Create one to assign a multi-state calendar to staff.
holidays.groupsHint: A group is a named bundle of states. Assign it to a staff member on their profile so the correct state holidays apply. Hold Ctrl (or Cmd) to select multiple states.
holidays.archetypeHint: Standard = official gazetted holidays only (national + the group’s states). Extended = official holidays plus company-defined extra days. Custom = only the holidays you hand-pick into this group; every other date, including national holidays, is a normal working day. Assign a group to staff on their profile (or map it to a location) and they follow exactly these rules.
holidays.parentGroupHint: A group with a parent automatically inherits the parent’s whole calendar — its gazette states, kind and extra days — and stays in sync when the parent changes. Add days that apply only to this group by adding a holiday with the “Holiday group” scope. One level of inheritance only: a parent cannot itself inherit from another group.
holidays.calendarEmpty: No holidays in this calendar yet.
holidays.calendarHint: Inherited days are read-only here — edit them at their source (the parent group, the public holiday list or the owning company). Days added to this group apply only to staff on this calendar.
holidays.editHint: Change any detail here and Save. Country stays as recorded. Leave and attendance follow the saved holiday automatically.
holidays.nationalStateHint: National applies to everyone. Choose a state to apply this holiday only to staff working in that state.
holidays.scopeFixedHint: This holiday belongs to a business group or holiday group. Its National / State cannot be changed here.

users.title: Users & roles
users.provisioningNote: New logins are created by invitation only — there is no open sign-up. An admin invites an existing employee by email, then WorkOS sends the one-time link and the invitee sets their own password. Only group admins can invite, archive or restore a login. Archiving blocks access without deleting anything, and a login is blocked automatically once every employment of that person has ended. Company scope applies to HR Admin grants — that company and its sub-companies; other roles are group-wide.
users.inviteHint: New accounts are created by invitation only — there is no open sign-up. The person receives a one-time email link to set their password.
users.functionAccessCaption: Which role can reach each screen. This mirrors the access the system enforces; it is a reference view, not an editor — changing enforcement lives in the role guards and database policies.

scope.people: Everyone can open this; the list is limited to the people you are allowed to see.
scope.leave: Everyone can open this; you see your own leave, managers and admins see their reports.
scope.leaveTracker: Everyone can open this; you see your own leave, managers see their reports, and administrators get the employee lookups instead of the calendar.
scope.attendance: Everyone can open this; you see your own attendance, managers and admins see their reports.
scope.myAttendanceRecords: Everyone can open this. It shows the reader their own attendance day by day, for a date range they choose, and never anybody else’s.
scope.myRoster: Everyone can open this. It shows the reader their own roster — the shifts their supervisor has planned for them — and never anybody else’s, whoever they are.
scope.approvals: Managers and above; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.roster: Managers and above; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.performance: Managers and above; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.leaveApproval: Managers and admins; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.payrollConfig: Everyone can open this; only admins for the company can change it.
scope.delegations: HR and admins see every delegation; you see only ones you delegated or cover.
scope.duplicatePersonRecords: Lists only employees in companies you administer, so half of a pair spanning two companies may not be visible to you. Read-only — no record can be changed from this screen.
scope.childReliefReview: Lists only current employees in companies you administer, so the ringgit totals are the totals of what you can see. Read-only — no tax setting can be changed from this screen.
scope.myTeam: Managers see their current direct or indirect reports. HR administrators can choose departments within their authorized companies.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.description: Every recorded change — who, what, when (append-only)

claims.title: Claims configuration
claims.subtitle: Define the expense/benefit claim types employees can submit, their default tax treatment, and optional budgets.
claims.empty: No claim types yet. Add one below.
claims.taxableHint: Default tax treatment seeds each claim; the approver confirms taxable vs non-taxable per claim. Taxable → next payslip (PCB); non-taxable → reimbursement.
claims.archiveConfirmDescription: Employees can no longer submit claims of this type. Existing claims are unaffected.
claims.itemArchiveConfirmDescription: It will no longer be selectable on new claims. Existing claims keep it.
claims.deleteConfirmDescription: This permanently deletes the claim type and its sub-categories and limits. Only possible when no claims have ever used it — otherwise archive it instead.
claims.limitsSubtitle: Configure claim eligibility and limits per Job Grade — reusing the grades already maintained for Leave.
claims.limitsMovedHint: Claim limits (per Job Grade) are configured on the Claim Limits tab.
claims.fallbackBadge: Falls back to the company-wide limit
claims.mileageSubtitle: Distance bands, vehicle type and rate per kilometre — per job grade, with an effective date.
claims.noMileageTable: No mileage rate table set here yet. Add distance bands below.
claims.mileageFallbackBadge: Inherited from the company-wide table. Saving below creates a table for this grade only.
claims.mileageEditorHint: Bands must run continuously from 0 km, and the last band must be left open (“and above”).
claims.mileageBandsHint: Rates are marginal: 700 km against 0–500 at 0.60 and 500+ at 0.45 pays 500×0.60 + 200×0.45.
claims.mileageStampHint: Changing a rate never changes a claim already submitted — each claim keeps the rate it was filed under.
claims.formsSubtitle: Choose what each claim type asks for. Fields you add appear on the employee’s claim form.
claims.builtInsHint: These four are part of how a claim is priced, checked against limits and paid, so they cannot be removed or reordered.
claims.noCustomFields: No extra fields. This claim type asks only for the four above.
claims.formsFooterHint: Removing a field takes it off new claims; answers already saved on filed claims are kept.
claims.isMileageHint: Only one claim type can be the mileage claim. Ticking it gives staff a distance box instead of an amount box, and tells Mileage Rates which claim type its distance bands belong to.
claims.noMileageType: No claim type is marked as the mileage claim yet, so there is nothing to set rates for.
claims.noMileageTypeLink: Go to Claim Types and tick one
claims.gridChangedOnly: Only the boxes you changed are written. Leave a box empty for no limit.
claims.gridSubHint: Anything claimed on a sub-claim still comes out of the {type} limit as well. An empty box means that sub-claim has no limit of its own.
claims.gridMileagePriced: Priced per kilometre on Mileage Rates
claims.gridMileageNoRate: No rate is asked for here.

reimbursements.title: Reimbursements due
reimbursements.subtitle: Approved non-taxable claims awaiting an off-cycle payout. Export a bank-upload file, transfer, then mark them paid. (Taxable claims are paid through payroll instead.)
reimbursements.empty: Nothing due. Approved non-taxable claims will appear here.
reimbursements.exportTitle: Download a neutral employee/bank/account/amount CSV for manual bank upload.
reimbursements.missingBankWarning: {count, plural, one {# claimant has no bank details on file — add them before exporting.} other {# claimants have no bank details on file — add them before exporting.}}
reimbursements.footnote: The CSV is a neutral list for manual upload, not a byte-exact bank giro file. Marking a claim paid is irreversible and records a domain event.

ai.title: AI configuration
ai.subtitle: Choose an AI provider and model and store your API key, to power Draft with AI on performance reviews.
ai.secretMissing: Set AI_CONFIG_SECRET on the server to store API keys securely. Until then, keys cannot be saved here.
ai.usingEnv: No provider is active for your organization — drafts use the platform default ({provider} · {model}).
ai.privacyNote: Draft with AI sends redacted review context — no names, emails, or ID numbers — to your chosen provider. It only proposes text; a manager always edits and submits.
ai.notStorable: Key storage is disabled until AI_CONFIG_SECRET is set on the server.
ai.makeActive: Use this provider for AI drafting

attendancePolicy.pageDescription: A centralized library of shift templates shared across your whole organisation. Create a shift once and assign it to any employee through their profile (fixed shift) or Roster Management.
attendancePolicy.policyPageDescription: The default working schedule each company falls back to when an employee has no roster for a date, plus the statutory overtime rates. Overtime is computed above the scheduled hours; a saved roster takes precedence.
attendancePolicy.lateHint: Check-in after “late after” is flagged late; check-out before “half-day before” is a half-day.
attendancePolicy.rosterNote: A person's usual shift is set as their Default shift on their profile (Personnel → Employment tab); the Roster screen is for date-specific exceptions. A rostered day overrides the default shift; employees with neither fall back to this default schedule.
attendancePolicy.dayTypeHint: Full = a normal working day. Half = a shorter working day (e.g. Saturday 9:00–12:00) — leave taken on it deducts 0.5 day by default, or 1.0 day if the half-day deduction setting is switched on. Rest = not a working day.
attendancePolicy.shiftTypeSemiFlexiNote: Semi-Flexi: employees may start any time within the window; breaks are always flexible with no clocking required.
attendancePolicy.shiftTypeFullFlexiNote: Full Flexi: the day is judged on total normal working hours, from whenever the employee clocks in. There is no lateness and no early out, and the times above are only the earliest and latest clocking accepted.
attendancePolicy.breakMismatchNote: Break windows shown for reference; the hours calculation deducts {minutes} min (the saved break total).
attendancePolicy.shiftPremiumHint: paid by payroll for working this shift — not an attendance calculation
attendancePolicy.shiftWorkingDaysDecidedBy: These days are set by the Schedule Group “{group}” and cannot be changed here. The shift keeps its own working week, and it comes back if the group stops stating one.
attendancePolicy.shiftHint: A shift ending at or before its start crosses midnight (⊕). The schedule drives attendance OT; no roster falls back to company policy.
attendancePolicy.multiBreakStorageHint: Multiple break windows are saved and shown, but the hours deducted still use their combined total — per-break precision is a future enhancement.
attendancePolicy.otApprovalCalcHint: When an overtime request is approved, this decides which figure becomes the approved overtime.
attendancePolicy.requireDeviceLabel: Require a registered device for web clocking
attendancePolicy.requireDeviceHint: When on, employees can clock in or out on the web only from a device they registered on the Clock in/out page. Terminal punch imports are unaffected. Leave off until your teams have registered their devices.
attendancePolicy.devicesIntro: Devices employees registered for web clocking. Revoking a device blocks clocking from it until the employee registers it again.
attendancePolicy.otRatesIntro: Overtime rates (the entitlement wage ceiling and the excess-hours multipliers) are managed here, alongside working hours and shifts. Payroll keeps using the same values; only the editing screen moved out of Payroll statutory settings.
attendancePolicy.coverageGap: {count} active employees have no backup shift. Their unrostered days are calculated from their company’s setting in Company Policy Settings.
attendancePolicy.coverageAllCovered: Every active employee has a backup shift, so no employee’s day is calculated from the company setting any more. It is still read for absence derivation and roster generation (which weekdays count as working days), and the overtime rates on this card are statutory and apply to everyone.
attendancePolicy.otWageCeilingLegalNote: The RM 4,000 wage ceiling is the Employment Act s.60A overtime-eligibility limit — a legal threshold, not a free operational rate. Change it only if the law changes.
attendancePolicy.otMultipliersNote: The 1.5× workday rate and the base-day pay (½/1-day rest-day, 2 days for a public holiday) are fixed by the Employment Act. The rest-day and public-holiday excess-hours rates default to the legal 2× / 3× and can be adjusted here.
attendancePolicy.otRulesHint: Shapes this shift's workday overtime: untick to disable OT, or set a minimum before OT counts and a daily cap. Statutory rates (1.5×/2×/3× and the RM4,000 ceiling) stay in Overtime rates above.
attendancePolicy.deleteShiftHint: Permanently delete a shift nothing uses. A shift used by a roster, as an employee's current shift, or anywhere in an employee's shift history — past included — must be archived instead.
attendancePolicy.ruleFieldWeekHint: This is the shift's Schedule Group. When the group states a working week of its own, the group — not this shift — decides which days are worked, and the Working days row above becomes read-only.
attendancePolicy.shiftNormalHoursRoundingHint: Normal hours are rounded DOWN to a multiple of this many minutes. Leave blank for no rounding.
attendancePolicy.shiftHalfDayHint: Set here, the 1st half-day clock-out becomes this shift's half-day cut-off. Left blank, the shift keeps the cut-off it uses today — its early-out grace before the shift end, or else the shift's midpoint. The company-wide half-day cut-off applies only to employees who have no shift.
attendancePolicy.shiftColorHint: The colour marks this shift on the Duty Roster so shifts can be told apart at a glance. Leave it unset and the roster colours this shift automatically, exactly as it does today.
attendancePolicy.shiftClockWindowHint: Time in and Time out are the hours the shift is worked. Shift Start Time and Shift Time Out are the earliest and the latest a clock-in or clock-out is accepted; tick Next day when the latest clock-out falls after midnight.
attendancePolicy.shiftClockWindowHintSemi: On a Semi Flexi shift, Flexi window start and Flexi window end are the span the employee may work within; the hours they must actually work are set below. Shift Start Time and Shift Time Out are the earliest and the latest a clock-in or clock-out is accepted; tick Next day when the latest clock-out falls after midnight.
attendancePolicy.shiftHalfDayPairHint: Used when an employee takes a half day: the 1st half end time is when the morning half ends, the 2nd half start time is when the afternoon half begins.
attendancePolicy.shiftTimeSequenceHint: Times are checked in sequence before a shift is saved: Shift Start Time cannot be after the time the shift starts, Shift Time Out cannot be before the time it ends, the 1st half end time must come before the 2nd half start time, every break must end after it starts and fall inside the shift, and a flexible break must be shorter than the shift.
attendancePolicy.recordedOnlyNote: saved and shown, but does not change any figure yet
attendancePolicy.otScheduleHint: Overtime is counted only inside these clock-time windows, each with its own shortest and longest length. “Adjust by” is signed: −30 takes half an hour off once the window reaches its threshold. Rounding and overtime rates stay with the Lateness, Early Out & Overtime rule. Leave the grid empty to keep counting overtime as the time worked past the shift end.
attendancePolicy.otScheduleNotInRound: Not included in this release: OT Shift, Next OT (if exceed max hours) and OT Allowance.
attendancePolicy.breakPaidHint: A paid break is not deducted from the shift’s hours; an unpaid one is. A break with no tick is unpaid, exactly as before.
attendancePolicy.generalMoreTabNote: The reference screen’s “General (More…)” tab was never captured, so its fields are not in this release.
attendancePolicy.shiftFormDescription: A shift template is shared across your whole organisation. Assign it to an employee through their profile (fixed shift) or Roster Management.

scheduleAssignment.pageDescription: Every employee's shift arrangement in force today, in one list. View / Edit opens the arrangement on its own page — the same record the employee's own profile shows, not a copy.
scheduleAssignment.statusScheduledHint: The earliest arrangement on file starts after today.
scheduleAssignment.statusNotRecordedHint: No dated arrangement on file yet.
scheduleAssignment.viewEditAria: View or edit the shift arrangement of {name}
scheduleAssignment.panelHint: Every employee has a backup shift — the shift used on any day they are not rostered. Fixed: they work it every working day, and the roster records only the exceptions. Roster: they are normally scheduled from the Roster screen, and the backup shift covers any day with no roster entry. A dated roster entry always wins; overtime and lateness are measured against whichever shift applies that day. Changing this does not alter attendance already recorded — it changes how days are calculated from now on. The change starts on the effective date you set; days before it keep the shift that was in force then.
scheduleAssignment.historyEmpty: No shift change has been recorded for this employee yet.
scheduleAssignment.panelMissing: That employee is no longer on this list. Clear the filters to find them.
scheduleAssignment.removeOnlyRefused: The only arrangement on file cannot be removed. Change it instead.
scheduleAssignment.removeNotFound: That arrangement is no longer on file.
scheduleAssignment.historyRemoveNote: Only the most recent change can be removed, and only while an earlier one is still on file: removing it puts back the arrangement that was in force before it. Earlier changes stay as they are — to alter one of those, save a new change instead.
scheduleAssignment.removeNotNewestRefused: Only the most recent change ({date}) can be removed. An earlier one cannot be put back once it is taken away — save a new change instead.
scheduleAssignment.removeConfirmBody: The arrangement that was in force before this change takes over again from that date, and attendance and overtime for those days are calculated against it. You can put this change back by saving it again.
scheduleAssignment.badEmployment: That employee could not be identified. Go back to the list, open them again and try once more.
scheduleAssignment.unexpectedError: The change could not be saved. Try again, and tell your system administrator if it keeps happening.
scheduleAssignment.activeOnlyNote: Active employees only. A leaver's shift history stays on their own profile.

filters.searchAria: Search employees by name or employee ID

scheduleAssignment.groupHint: Choose the schedule group first. It decides this employee’s lateness, early-out and overtime rules, and it limits which shifts can be assigned below. Leave it blank and those rules come from the shift they are on, exactly as before.
scheduleAssignment.groupLibraryEmpty: No schedule groups exist yet. Create one on the Schedule Group screen, and list the shifts it allows.
scheduleAssignment.narrowedByGroup: {hidden, plural, =0 {Every shift in the library belongs to “{group}”, so nothing is hidden.} one {The list shows only the shifts allowed by “{group}”. # other shift is not offered.} other {The list shows only the shifts allowed by “{group}”. # other shifts are not offered.}}
scheduleAssignment.groupAllowsNothing: The schedule group “{group}” does not allow any shift yet, so none can be chosen. Add shifts to that group on the Schedule Group screen first.
scheduleAssignment.bulkDescription: Put many employees in the same schedule group in one action. Filter the list, tick the people, choose the group and apply. Either every one of them is moved or none is: if one employee is already on a shift the group does not allow, nothing is saved and the message names them.
scheduleAssignment.bulkSelected: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody selected} one {# employee selected} other {# employees selected}}
scheduleAssignment.bulkConfirmBody: The schedule group decides the lateness, early-out and overtime rules these employees are measured against from now on. Attendance already recorded is not recalculated. Nobody’s shift is changed. If one of them is on a shift the group does not allow, nothing is saved at all.
scheduleAssignment.bulkDoneNote: {changed, plural, =0 {Nothing to change — everybody selected was already in that schedule group.} one {# employee moved into that schedule group.} other {# employees moved into that schedule group.}}{unchanged, plural, =0 {} one { # was already in it.} other { # were already in it.}}
scheduleAssignment.bulkHint: Only the employees shown are affected. Narrow the filters above to change who “select all” means.

payrollPermissions.title: Payroll & leave permissions
payrollPermissions.subtitle: Granular permissions for high-risk actions — payroll runs, and applying for leave on behalf of another employee — configurable per company or tenant-wide.
payrollPermissions.defaultsHint: These are the built-in defaults. This screen is not payroll-only — every granular permission the system enforces is listed above, whichever part of the product it belongs to. Add an override below to widen or narrow who holds a permission for a specific company or tenant-wide.
payrollPermissions.overridesEmpty: No overrides — the defaults above apply.

toilPolicy.pageDescription: Let rest-day, holiday, or overtime work be banked as replacement leave instead of paid as cash, per company. Contractual, not statutory: a worked day is paid or banked, never both.
toilPolicy.moduleOff: Time off in lieu is not part of this account's plan. You can review policies here, but no new time will be banked.
toilPolicy.moduleOffWindDown: Time off in lieu is not part of this account's plan, so no new time is being banked. {accruals} banked credit(s) are still outstanding and can still be settled below — days already earned are never forfeited by a plan change.
toilPolicy.enabledLabel: Enable time off in lieu for this company
toilPolicy.enabledHint: When on, managers can bank a worked rest day or holiday as replacement leave from the roster.
toilPolicy.allowEligibleHint: Statutory overtime pay normally applies to these employees. If enabled, banking is allowed but unused time always converts to pay on expiry (never lapses), and a compliance note is shown. Confirm with counsel.
toilPolicy.footnote: Taking time in lieu is a normal leave request against the Replacement Leave type. Public holidays and rosters are unaffected.
toilPolicy.processHint: Convert or lapse time in lieu past its expiry, following each accrual's frozen rule. Runs for today; a scheduled job will automate this later.
toilPolicy.processedBanner: Processed {processed} expirations: {converted} converted to pay, {lapsed} lapsed.
toilPolicy.processedNone: No time in lieu was due for expiry.
toilPolicy.processedSkipped: {skipped} further expiry(ies) were due but belong to a company you do not administer — they were left unsettled. An administrator for those companies must run this sweep.
toilPolicy.autoAccrueLabel: Auto-create credit when attendance is approved
toilPolicy.autoAccrueHint: When on, approving a rest-day or public-holiday attendance correction automatically banks the replacement leave — no manual roster election needed.
toilPolicy.carryForwardLabel: Carry forward unused credit at year-end
toilPolicy.carryForwardHint: When on, unused replacement leave survives the year-end close instead of expiring. The choice is frozen on each credit when it is banked.
toilPolicy.ledgerHint: Active days still available versus those taken, expired, or converted to pay, across everyone in scope.
toilPolicy.closeYearHint: Expire (or carry forward, per each credit's frozen rule) the remaining replacement leave at the year boundary. A supervised once-a-year action; run before opening the new leave year.
toilPolicy.closeBanner: Year closed: {processed} credits swept — {converted} converted to pay, {lapsed} lapsed, {carried} carried forward.
toilPolicy.closeAlready: This year boundary was already closed; nothing to do.
toilPolicy.configMovedHint: The policy editor for replacement leave now lives under Leave Config.

locations.pageDescription: Every company you administer, and the work locations it maintains.
locations.name: Name
locations.clockingDescription: Authorized sites employees may clock in and out from. A clocking location is created once and is available to every company; assign sites and geofencing per employee on their profile.
locations.deleteConfirmDescription: Delete “{name}” permanently? This cannot be undone. Only possible when no employee is assigned and no attendance record references it.
locations.clockingInUse: Cannot delete: referenced by {count} record(s). Archive it instead.
locations.clockingNote: Deleting is only possible when a site has no employee assignments and no attendance history. Otherwise, archive it.
locations.radiusNote: Each clocking point carries its own allowed distance, so a tight office and a wide project yard can both be right. We warn outside 10–5000 m but never block the save.
locations.radiusWarningTight: Saved. A radius of {radius} m is unusually tight — phone GPS is rarely accurate to better than 10 m, so staff may be refused while standing on site.
locations.radiusWarningWide: Saved. A radius of {radius} m is unusually wide — anyone within that distance of the point can clock in.
locations.groupNoPoints: This location has no geofenced clocking points yet — clock-in is unavailable at this site.
locations.unmappedBranchesHeading: Branches with no location mapped yet
locations.unmappedBranchRow: {branch} — {count} staff, no work location can be proposed for them
locations.branchTaken: {branch} is already mapped to location {code} in this company. A branch can only be mapped to one location — clear it there first, or choose another branch.
locations.branchTakenNoCode: {branch} is already mapped to another location in this company. A branch can only be mapped to one location.
locations.codeTaken: A location with code {code} already exists. Location codes must be unique — choose a different one.
locations.sharedManagedByGroupAdmin: Shared clocking locations are created and edited by a group administrator. You can still assign any of them to your employees on each employee’s profile.
locations.linkedOutOfScopeGroupTitle: Linked to a location outside your company scope
locations.clockingNameTaken: A clocking location named “{name}” already exists. Names are unique across all companies — one record per physical place — so edit that one or choose a different name.
locations.reportLabelHint: The report label is what the Attendance report prints in its Clocking Location column instead of the full name. Leave it blank and the name is used.
locations.addressSearchHint: Type an address and press Search, then pick a result to fill in the address, latitude and longitude. You can still type all three by hand.
locations.addressSearchEmpty: Type an address to search for.
locations.addressSearchNoResults: No match found. Try a simpler address, or type the coordinates by hand.
locations.addressSearchFailed: Address search is unavailable right now. Type the address and coordinates by hand.
locations.addressSearchPicked: Address, latitude and longitude filled in. Check the marker on the map before saving.
locations.mapUnavailable: The map could not be loaded. Latitude, longitude and radius can still be typed in and saved.
locations.mapNoPoint: Enter a latitude and longitude to see the point and its clocking radius.
locations.mapSatelliteUnavailable: Satellite view is off: every supplier of satellite imagery needs a paid account. Send us a map key and it switches on here.
locations.mapManualHint: The map is a preview. The boxes above are what gets saved.
locations.statusLegend: Active means this company has at least one location that is not archived. Inactive means it has none — use Add to give it one.
locations.branchHint: Mapping a branch lets the Personnel Attendance tab propose this location for the staff who carry it.
locations.clockingPointsAfterSave: Clocking points can be added once this location has been saved.
locations.offRegisterTitle: Clocking points not linked to a location
locations.offRegisterDescription: These clocking points are not attached to any location you can see, so they are maintained here rather than on a location’s own screen.
locations.offRegisterLink: {count} clocking points are not linked to a location
locations.archivedNote: This location is archived. It is kept for history and can be restored.

profileOptions.title: Profile Options
profileOptions.subtitle: Manage the dropdown values for employee profile fields (religion, race, nationality, state, country, relationship).
profileOptions.emptyAll: No profile options yet. Add the default set to get started.
profileOptions.deleteDescription: Delete "{value}"? This cannot be undone. An option in use by an employee cannot be deleted — deactivate it instead.
profileOptions.legacyNote: Existing employee records keep their stored value even if it is not in this list; you can still save without changing it.
profileOptions.saveFailed: Some changes could not be saved. Check the highlighted rows.
profileOptions.codeImmutableHint: The code is permanent once created.

holidayGroups.pageDescription: Reusable holiday collections you can assign to employees on their profile
holidayGroups.empty: No holiday groups yet. Create one to assign a shared holiday calendar to staff.
holidayGroups.statesHint: The group automatically includes the public holidays of these Malaysian states. Hold Ctrl (or Cmd) to select multiple.
holidayGroups.archetypeHint: Standard = official gazetted holidays only. Extended = official holidays plus company-defined extra days. Custom = only the holidays you hand-pick.
