holidayGroups.parentGroupHint: A group with a parent inherits the parent's whole calendar and stays in sync when the parent changes. One level of inheritance only.
holidayGroups.holidaysSectionHint: Tick the holidays from the master list that belong to this group. Automatic Malaysian state holidays still apply on top of your selection.
holidayGroups.noHolidays: No holidays in the master list yet. Add holidays on the Holiday tab first.

holidayCoverage.warnEmptyTitle: This calendar holds no public holidays
holidayCoverage.warnEmptyBody: A work location attached to “{name}” gives its staff exactly the days ticked into this calendar and nothing else, and nothing is ticked. All {gazette} public holidays gazetted for {year} would be ordinary working days for them — counted against their leave, and paid at the ordinary overtime rate:
holidayCoverage.warnMissingTitle: This calendar leaves out {missing, plural, =1 {# gazetted day} other {# gazetted days}}
holidayCoverage.warnMissingBody: “{name}” holds {held} of the {gazette} public holidays gazetted for {year}. A work location attached to it gives its staff exactly those days, so these would be ordinary working days for them:
holidayCoverage.note: This is a warning, not a block. A calendar that deliberately holds fewer days is a real thing, and you can still save it.
holidayCoverage.okLine: “{name}” holds all {gazette} public holidays gazetted for {year}.

attendanceRule.moduleDescription: A reusable library of attendance calculation rules. Assign a rule to a shift, or let shifts fall back to the Standard rule.
attendanceRule.libraryIntro: Each rule bundles Lateness, Early Out and Overtime settings. Rules are shared across every company — the shift picks the rule, and the Standard rule applies when a shift chooses none.
attendanceRule.scheduleSectionIntro: The working hours below apply only on a day where the employee has no shift assigned; on any day with a shift, that shift decides. The overtime rates apply to your whole organisation.
attendanceRule.formDescription: Configure how lateness, early-out and overtime are calculated.
attendanceRule.standardNote: This is the Standard rule. It cannot be deleted and its name is fixed, but you can edit its settings.
attendanceRule.includeGraceInEarlyOut: Include Grace Period into Early Out
attendanceRule.applyEarlyOtHint: Counts every minute clocked before the scheduled start time as overtime. There is no approval step — with this on, an early arrival earns overtime automatically.
attendanceRule.otEmptyHint: No overtime bands yet. Use + Add Row to define how overtime is calculated.
attendanceRule.statutoryCapNote: Statutory overtime multipliers (1.5×, 2×, 3×) remain the legal minimum and are set in the company overtime rates. These rules shape and round overtime on top of that.
attendanceRule.otRoundToHint: Minutes to round to — for example 5, 10 or 15. Must be at least 1.
attendanceRule.applyDeductionsLabel: Apply the lateness and early-out deductions
attendanceRule.applyDeductionsHint: Off by default. Turning this on records a deduction for late arrivals and early departures from today onward — days already worked are never changed.
attendanceRule.otLadderGapWarning: Row {row} must start at {expected} minutes to continue from row {prev} — it starts at {actual}. Saving is blocked until the rows join up.
attendanceRule.otLadderOpenEndedWarning: Row {row} has no upper limit, so no row can follow it. Give it a “To” value or move it to the end.
attendanceRule.shiftsAllowedHint: The shifts that follow this group’s lateness, early-out and overtime rules. A shift belongs to exactly one group, so ticking one here moves it out of the group it is in now; unticking one leaves it on the Standard group.
attendanceRule.shiftsAllowedEmpty: There are no shifts to choose from yet.

benefitScheme.groupsHelp: Group several grades so one rule can cover them at once (e.g. "Grade 12–15"). Approval rules and employee eligibility both name grade groups. A grade belongs to one group.
benefitScheme.thresholdError: Tier boundaries must be whole numbers with the second greater than the first.
benefitScheme.dragHint: Drag a row onto another to group leave types under one shared total limit. Drop a row onto a group to move it there.
benefitScheme.dropGradeHint: Drag a grade from the Grade Master onto a group to add it — or tick its checkbox inside the group and save.
benefitScheme.maxDaysPerApplicationHelp: Optional. Leave blank for no limit. Set it to 3 and no single application for any leave type in this group may cover more than 3 calendar days — separately from the shared yearly total.

systemExplorer.title: System analysis & dependency explorer
systemExplorer.description: How this product is put together: pick a record type to see what points at it, what it points at, and which module owns it. Read from the live database every time, so it is never out of date. Structure only — no record data is shown.
systemExplorer.formNote: {count} record types in this installation. Related types are links — follow one to move across the map.
systemExplorer.unknownTable: There is no record type called “{table}” in this installation.
systemExplorer.noReferences: This record type does not point at anything.
systemExplorer.noReferencedBy: Nothing points at this record type.
systemExplorer.withheldNote: {count} record types are not listed. They hold encryption keys, signing keys, provider credentials or sign-in tokens, so their structure is deliberately withheld.
systemExplorer.withheldEdges: {count} relationships to withheld record types are not shown here.

replacementLeave.enabledLabel: Enable replacement leave for this company
replacementLeave.enabledHint: Approved rest-day and public-holiday overtime can be banked as replacement leave instead of paid as cash.
replacementLeave.expiryHint: Counted from the date the line manager approves the credit. Months are counted as calendar months. Both counts are kept, so switching the unit and switching back does not lose the other one. Changing this affects only credits granted afterwards — credits already held keep the period they were granted under.
replacementLeave.leaveFromRecordedOnly: Recorded only. This setting is stored for your records and changes nothing today — no attendance, timesheet or overtime figure is checked against it, and it does not affect what is banked.
replacementLeave.allowEligibleLabel: Allow employees within the First Schedule
replacementLeave.allowEligibleHint: Employees at or below the statutory overtime wage ceiling are legally entitled to overtime cash rather than banked time. With this on they may bank it instead, but only with their own recorded agreement, and unused credit always converts to pay on expiry rather than lapsing.
replacementLeave.autoAccrueLabel: Bank automatically when an attendance correction is approved
replacementLeave.autoAccrueHint: Approving a rest-day or public-holiday attendance correction banks the credit without a separate election from the roster.
replacementLeave.carryForwardHint: Credits survive the year-end close instead of expiring. Frozen onto each credit when it is granted, so changing this later does not alter credits already held.
replacementLeave.employeeRequestLabel: Let employees submit their own replacement leave requests
replacementLeave.employeeRequestHint: When this is off, employees do not see the request button and cannot submit a request.
replacementLeave.eligibilityHint: Leave every picker empty to allow everyone. Otherwise an employee qualifies if they are named individually, or if they match every criterion you have set. Departments, positions and employment types are matched against the assignment the employee held on the day they submit.
replacementLeave.footnote: Replacement leave credits are granted with their expiry date fixed at the moment they are approved. Changing any setting here affects only credits granted afterwards.
replacementLeave.extendedEnabledLabel: Credit extended hours worked on an ordinary working day
replacementLeave.extendedEnabledHint: Off by default. When on, time worked past the scheduled shift end on an ordinary working day can earn a Leave Credit. That day’s overtime is then NOT also paid — the day is given back as leave instead. Early clock-in before the shift starts never counts.
replacementLeave.extendedHint: The break and the grace period come off the time worked past the shift end first; what is left decides the credit. Below the half-day threshold nothing is earned — there is no part credit. At or above it, half a day. At or above the full-day threshold, one day, and one day is the most any single date can earn. This applies only to ordinary working days; a rest day, off day or public holiday is unchanged and still uses the accrual basis above.

entitlementArchive.pageDescription: A read-only record of the entitlement tables and benefit schemes captured before a reset cleared them.
entitlementArchive.intro: This is the written record of every entitlement figure currently configured, taken before anything can be cleared. Each row shows what was set up, who it applied to and what it was worth, so the figures can be read off here and retyped into the new entitlement tables rather than remembered.
entitlementArchive.notAnUndo: This is a listing to retype from, not an undo button. Restoring the old setup means entering it again.
entitlementArchive.feedsNothing: It feeds nothing and changes no number. No balance, no entitlement and no leave record is affected by anything on this page.
entitlementArchive.emptyBody: The record is taken automatically before a reset clears anything. If this is empty, there was no entitlement configuration to record.

leaveLedgerArchive.pageDescription: A read-only record of every balance record removed by a reset, kept so the old figures are never lost.
leaveLedgerArchive.intro: This is the written record taken immediately before a reset removed anything. Each reset writes its own record; choose the one to read below. Each row shows who held the record, which leave type it belonged to, how many days it was worth, the date it took effect and why it was there.
leaveLedgerArchive.notAnUndo: This is a record to read from, not an undo button. The rows listed here were removed and putting them back means entering them again.
leaveLedgerArchive.feedsNothing: It feeds nothing and changes no number. No balance, no entitlement and no leave record is affected by anything on this page.
leaveLedgerArchive.noLeaveHistory: No leave anybody applied for or was approved for was removed. Every reset here kept the days people had actually taken, so no leave history is affected.
leaveLedgerArchive.emptyBody: The record is written by each reset itself, before anything is removed. If this is empty, no reset has been run on this system.
leaveLedgerArchive.counts: {ledger} balance records and {audit} recalculation history entries in this record.

entitlementTemplates.pageDescription: Write a service-based entitlement table once, then say who gets it.
entitlementTemplates.intro: An entitlement table lists your own service ranges and the days each one earns. Write it once, name it, and let as many benefit schemes name it as you like, instead of retyping the same table inside every scheme.
entitlementTemplates.coexistNote: A benefit scheme is optional: one is only needed to choose between several entitlement tables. Where a benefit scheme covers an employee, the table it names decides their days; schemes are set on the Leave types tab, on the leave type they belong to. A leave type with a single table and no scheme applies that table to everyone. Anyone no scheme covers receives the leave type’s default entitlement table, where one is named.
entitlementTemplates.gridOverlapNote: One row per table and service range. Where more than one benefit scheme could cover the same employee, the one with narrower conditions decides, so a person may appear in two rows and receive only one of them. To see what a named person actually gets, and why, use the panel below.
entitlementTemplates.gridNoGrade: Nobody — no benefit scheme names this table
entitlementTemplates.datedNote: Both tables and schemes carry a start date, and that date decides what Save does. Leave the date alone and the version you are editing is updated in place, including one that is already in force. Give it a later date and the running version is closed on that date and a new one starts, so a report for a closed year still reads the figures that were in force back then. A version that has not started yet is always corrected in place.
entitlementTemplates.filterHint: Showing all leave types side by side. Choose one to see only its tables — and to be warned when a new table would reach nobody.
entitlementTemplates.filterHintScoped: Showing the tables for {type}. Clear the filter to see every leave type side by side, which is what this tab is for.
entitlementTemplates.supersedeNote: This version is already in force. Give it a LATER date and saving closes it on that date and starts a new one, so nothing already worked out changes. Save without changing the date and this version is updated in place.
entitlementTemplates.editInPlaceNote: This version has not started yet, so saving changes it in place, its effective date included. Give it a date in the past and it takes effect from that date, which changes what a past leave year says — only do that to correct a date that was keyed wrongly.
entitlementTemplates.refuseNote: This version has been in force since {from}, so its start date cannot be moved earlier. Keep {from} to update this version in place, or choose a later date to close it and start a new one.
entitlementTemplates.inPlaceInForceNote: The date has not changed, so saving updates the version you are looking at — nothing is closed and no new version is created. Give it a LATER date instead and this version is closed on that date and a new one starts.
entitlementTemplates.inPlaceStartedWarning: This version has been in force since {from}. Updating it in place also changes what closed leave years report, because entitlement is worked out at a past date by the Carry Forward report, the year-end expiry sweep and every balance breakdown. Give it a later date instead to leave those figures alone.
entitlementTemplates.createNoRuleWarning: {type} has no benefit scheme in force and no default entitlement table, so a table saved here reaches no employee until a scheme below names it, or until you make it the default.
entitlementTemplates.createEndsSoleTableWarning: {type} has a single entitlement table and no benefit scheme, so that table currently applies to everyone. Saving a second table ends that: from then on NEITHER table reaches anybody until a benefit scheme names them, or one of them is set as the default entitlement table for {type}.
entitlementTemplates.stopTemplateConfirm: From that date this table hands out nothing, and the {rules} benefit schemes naming it stop covering anybody. Nothing is deleted and no leave record changes.
entitlementTemplates.bandCeiling: Leave the last To year(s) blank for no limit. Up to {max} ranges.
entitlementTemplates.rulesIntro: A benefit scheme says who receives which entitlement table, from when. It is what the employee's profile shows as their Benefit Scheme.
entitlementTemplates.rulesNone: No benefit schemes yet. A scheme is only needed to choose between several entitlement tables — a leave type with one table, or with a default table named, reaches everybody without one.
entitlementTemplates.rulesNeedTemplate: Create an entitlement table on the Entitlement tables screen first, because a scheme has to name one.
entitlementTemplates.stopRuleConfirm: From that date this scheme covers nobody. Nothing is deleted and no leave record changes.
entitlementTemplates.deleteTemplateConfirm: This removes the table and every version of it for good. It can be deleted because no benefit scheme names it and no entitlement was granted while it was in force. Deleting cannot be undone — stop it from a date instead if you may want it back.
entitlementTemplates.deleteRuleConfirm: This removes the scheme and every version of it for good. It can be deleted because no entitlement was granted while it was in force. Deleting cannot be undone — stop it from a date instead if you may want it back.
entitlementTemplates.deleteBlockedByRules: Cannot delete while a benefit scheme names this table: {rules}. Delete the scheme first, or stop this table from a date.
entitlementTemplates.ruleCheckHint: Check who this reaches before saving.
entitlementTemplates.ruleMatchedCount: {count} employees match on the effective date.
entitlementTemplates.ruleEveryoneWarning: No restrictions are set, so this scheme covers everyone.
entitlementTemplates.ruleUndatedAxesNote: Department, position, business unit, cost centre, location and employment type are read as they were on the date being asked about. Grade, gender, nationality, religion and race are not dated in this system, so they are always read at today's value.
entitlementTemplates.ruleJobGradeHint: Your Job Grade labels, read live from System Labels. Archive one there and it disappears from here.
entitlementTemplates.ruleGradeGroupNote: Picking a grade group fills in the job grades it holds today. If a grade joins that group later, this rule keeps the grades it was saved with until you pick the group again.
entitlementTemplates.ruleGradeGroupPartial: This rule covers only part of {groups}. Pick the group again to take in every grade it holds — until then it cannot be assigned to an approval template.
entitlementTemplates.healthTitle: Can this leave type produce a balance?
entitlementTemplates.healthCardHelp: Every active leave type, and what is still missing before it can produce a balance. A leave type marked Cannot grant shows 0.00 for everybody today.
entitlementTemplates.healthCounts: Earning method: {method} · Entitlement tables in force: {tables} · Benefit schemes in force: {rules}
entitlementTemplates.healthSoleTable: The single table applies to everyone, so no benefit scheme is needed.
entitlementTemplates.healthNoEarningMethod: No earning method chosen, so nothing is granted however complete the tables are.
entitlementTemplates.healthNoEntitlementTable: No entitlement table has been set up, so there is no number of days to grant.
entitlementTemplates.healthNoRuleInForce: {tables} entitlement tables, no benefit scheme in force and no default table named, so no employee resolves to any of them.
entitlementTemplates.healthConfiguredVsActual: Configured: {configured} days across {tables} entitlement tables in force. None of them reaches anybody, because no benefit scheme in force names them and no default table is set - so the entitlement run grants nothing from this configuration. Days already on an employee’s record came from an earlier configuration or were entered by hand.
entitlementTemplates.healthTableWithoutRule: No benefit scheme names: {tables}. Nobody receives them until a scheme names one, or one of them becomes this leave type’s default table.
entitlementTemplates.healthReplacementLeaveHasEntitlementTabl: Leave Credit is switched on, so every day of this leave type should come from Leave Credit. An entitlement table in force still adds days nobody earned: {tables}. Remove the table.
entitlementTemplates.healthRuleExpired: Benefit scheme expired, so it covers nobody: {rules}
entitlementTemplates.healthGradesWithoutTable: Job grades that belong to no entitlement table: {grades}
entitlementTemplates.healthMaxBalanceZero: Maximum Balance is 0, which cancels the days granted: {tables}
entitlementTemplates.healthEarnedMethodNotAnnualLeave: Set to earn its days through Earned Accrual, but Earned Accrual applies only to Annual Leave, so no days are added to this leave type. Change its earning method so the days are granted up front, or switch on “This is our Annual Leave” if this is your Annual Leave.
entitlementTemplates.ruleTargetStopped: {table} — stopped, so this scheme reaches nobody
entitlementTemplates.inheritedTitle: Already set on the leave type (Who is eligible tab)
entitlementTemplates.inheritedNote: These conditions decide whether an employee may take this leave at all, and they already apply to every scheme below. Do not repeat them here — what you set below decides only WHICH entitlement table an eligible employee gets.
entitlementTemplates.inheritedNone: This leave type sets no conditions of its own, so it is open to every employee. Everything below decides only which entitlement table they get.
entitlementTemplates.rulesNamingTip: Tip: use the same scheme name on every leave type it covers, and the employee's profile shows that one name.
entitlementTemplates.ruleEveryoneTitle: One scheme for everyone this leave type is available to
entitlementTemplates.ruleEveryoneHelp: A scheme with no conditions of its own: everyone who passes the leave type’s own conditions gets the entitlement table you pick. Use it whenever one table fits everybody.
entitlementTemplates.ruleEveryoneCount: This assigns the table to {count} employees on the effective date — everyone the leave type is available to.
entitlementTemplates.ruleEveryoneConfirm: This scheme sets no conditions of its own, so it covers everyone the leave type is available to, and balances are recalculated as soon as it is saved.
entitlementTemplates.soleTableNoRuleNeeded: No scheme is needed for {types}: each has a single entitlement table and no benefit scheme, so that table already applies to everyone the leave type is available to. Nothing is missing here.
entitlementTemplates.explainTitle: Why does an employee get this table, or none?
entitlementTemplates.explainHelp: Search for an employee and pick a leave type. This names the benefit schemes that exist, says which are in force, and for each one in force gives the first thing about that employee which does not match.
entitlementTemplates.explainSearchLabel: Employee name, employee ID or email
entitlementTemplates.explainMatchesMore: Showing the first {count} matches. Narrow the search to see the rest.
entitlementTemplates.explainWinnerSole: Resolves to {table}. This leave type has one entitlement table and no benefit scheme, so the table applies to everyone — no scheme is needed.
entitlementTemplates.explainNoWinner: No entitlement table resolves for this employee.
entitlementTemplates.explainNotActive: This employee was not employed on {date} — hired later, or already terminated — so no scheme can cover them on that date.
entitlementTemplates.explainNoRules: This leave type has no benefit schemes at all.
entitlementTemplates.explainSentence: {facts, select, both {{employee} is {grade} with {years, plural, =1 {# year} other {# years}} of service. } grade {{employee} is {grade}. } years {{employee} has {years, plural, =1 {# year} other {# years}} of service. } other {}}The scheme “{rule}”{hasClause, select, yes { ({clause})} other {}} covers them, and its table {table} {hasDays, select, yes {gives {days, plural, =1 {# day} other {# days}}{band, select, open { for {from} or more years of service} closed { for {from} to {to} years of service} other {}}} other {applies}}.
entitlementTemplates.explainSentenceDefault: {facts, select, both {{employee} is {grade} with {years, plural, =1 {# year} other {# years}} of service. } grade {{employee} is {grade}. } years {{employee} has {years, plural, =1 {# year} other {# years}} of service. } other {}}No benefit scheme describes them, so this leave type’s default entitlement table {table} applies{hasDays, select, yes {, and it gives {days, plural, =1 {# day} other {# days}}{band, select, open { for {from} or more years of service} closed { for {from} to {to} years of service} other {}}} other {}}.

entitlementTemplates.explainWhyChosenSpecific: Chosen over “{other}” because its conditions are narrower.
entitlementTemplates.explainWhyChosenLater: {basis, select, start {Ties with “{other}” on how many conditions it narrows by, so the one that takes effect later wins — this one starts {date}.} other {Ties with “{other}” on both the conditions and the start date {date}, so the one set up most recently wins. Give one of them narrower conditions or a later start date to make the choice deliberate.}}
entitlementTemplates.explainWhyChosenArbitrary: Ties with “{other}” on every test the system uses — the same number of conditions, the same start date {date}, and both set up at the same moment. Nothing chose between them, so this one won by chance and could win differently tomorrow. Give one of them narrower conditions or a later start date.
entitlementTemplates.explainStateTableStopped: Its entitlement table is stopped, so it reaches nobody
entitlementTemplates.explainWhyCombination: Every condition passes on its own, but not all of them on the same assignment record — check department, position, business unit, cost centre, location and employment type together.
entitlementTemplates.explainWhyNotTested: Not compared against this employee on this date.
entitlementTemplates.defaultTableIntro: Used for anyone no benefit scheme covers. A scheme chooses between this leave type’s tables; the default is what an employee no scheme names receives, so nobody is left without an entitlement table. Leave it unset and an employee no scheme covers receives nothing, exactly as before.
entitlementTemplates.defaultTableNone: No default — anyone no scheme covers receives nothing
entitlementTemplates.defaultTableNoTables: There is no entitlement table in force on this leave type yet, so there is nothing to name as the default.
entitlementTemplates.createWithDefaultTableNote: {type} has no benefit scheme in force, and {table} is its default entitlement table — so everyone receives {table} today. A table saved here reaches nobody until a scheme names it, or until you make it the default instead.
entitlementTemplates.healthDefaultTable: Anyone no benefit scheme covers receives the default table {table}.
entitlementTemplates.explainWinnerDefault: Resolves to {table}, the default entitlement table for this leave type. No benefit scheme covers this employee, so the default applies — entitlement is not withheld because a scheme is missing.
entitlementTemplates.coversDefaultTable: Anyone no benefit scheme covers — this leave type’s default table
entitlementTemplates.uncoveredHelp: Leave types that have an entitlement table in force, where no benefit scheme describes this employee and the leave type has no default table either. Nothing is granted and nothing is invented. A scheme is a description — a job grade, a department, a length of service — not a list of names, so the fix is to widen or add a scheme whose description covers these people, or to give the leave type a default entitlement table.
entitlementTemplates.uncoveredNone: Every active employee is reached by an entitlement table on every leave type that has one.
entitlementTemplates.uncoveredNoGrade: {count} of these have no job grade recorded at all, out of {total} active employees. A benefit scheme that matches on job grade can never reach them — the grades have to be filled in on the employment records.

benefitScheme.title: Benefit Scheme
benefitScheme.none: Does not resolve to a single scheme
benefitScheme.noneHint: This employee is picked up by different schemes for different leave types, so there is no one scheme to name. What applies to each leave type is listed below.
benefitScheme.noRule: No scheme rule — the only table for this leave type
benefitScheme.empty: No benefit scheme covers this employee, and no leave type names a default entitlement table they could fall back to — so no table reaches them. A scheme decides which entitlement table an employee receives; it is not what decides whether they are entitled.
benefitScheme.derivedNote: Worked out automatically from the benefit schemes on the Leave types screen. There is nothing to set here: a benefit scheme decides which entitlement table this employee receives. It does not decide whether they are eligible for a leave type, and it never grants or removes days by itself.
benefitScheme.derivedNoteEmpty: Worked out automatically from the benefit schemes on the Leave types screen. There is nothing to set here: a scheme on each leave type says who it covers, and each leave type can also name a default entitlement table for everyone a scheme does not.
benefitScheme.setUpSchemes: Set up benefit schemes on the Leave types screen
benefitScheme.notCoveredHint: Receives the default entitlement table for each leave type, listed below.
benefitScheme.derivedNoteDefault: Worked out automatically from the benefit schemes on the Leave types screen. There is nothing to set here: a benefit scheme is optional, and where none covers this employee they receive the default entitlement table chosen for each leave type. Entitlement is never withheld because a scheme is missing.
benefitScheme.unmatchedWarning: Needs your attention: no entitlement table reaches this employee for {types}. No benefit scheme’s conditions match this employee for those leave types, and no default entitlement table is set for them. No days have been assigned, and none will be invented.
benefitScheme.unmatchedNoGrade: This employee has no job grade recorded, so a benefit scheme that matches on job grade can never reach them.

leaveConfigRecords.pageDescription: The written records taken before each reset cleared entitlement configuration or balances. Read-only: nothing here changes a number.

leaveConfigTypes.rowDescription: Each leave type, what it entitles an employee to, and who receives which table.

tabHint.identity: What this leave type is called, and how it behaves.
tabHint.eligibility: Who may take this leave at all. Leave a field empty to mean anyone.
tabHint.entitlement: How many days, and who receives which table.
tabHint.application: What an application for this leave type has to satisfy. Each card saves on its own.
tabHint.approvers: The approval settings that belong to the leave type itself. Approval chains are built and assigned on the Approval chain screen.

entitlementStep.schemeExplainer: Eligibility (the Who is eligible tab) decides whether an employee can take this leave type. A benefit scheme decides WHICH entitlement table an employee receives where there is more than one; anyone no scheme covers receives the default entitlement table named here.

leaveConfigBalanceHealth.pageDescription: Which leave types can produce a balance today, and what is missing before the rest can.

leaveConfigAdjustments.pageDescription: Change an employee's balance by hand, see what was changed, and load balances from a file.

leaveConfigGenerate.pageDescription: Run the entitlement for a leave year, preview it first, and read the log of every run.

leaveConfigEarnedAccrual.pageDescription: Top up the entitlement already earned and not yet posted — preview the dry run first, then confirm.

leaveConfigCompanyRules.pageDescription: The leave settings that belong to a company or to the whole organisation, gathered in one place.
leaveConfigCompanyRules.intro: The leave settings here belong to a company or to the whole organisation rather than to any one leave type, so they are set once instead of being repeated on every leave type.
leaveConfigCompanyRules.whoQualifies: Who may take a leave type, and who receives which entitlement table, is set under Leave types, not here.

leaveConfigSpecialSetting.pageDescription: Settings that apply across every leave type rather than belonging to any one of them.

leaveConfigApprovalChains.pageDescription: Build an approval flow once, decide who it applies to, and see every rule that decides who signs off.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.scopesTitle: Rules with their own scope or chain
leaveConfigApprovalChains.scopesHint: These active rules either narrow to a business unit, department or position — which the assignment list above does not show — or carry their own steps instead of a template. Both decide who approves a request, so each is listed here with the chain that actually applies.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.scopesReadOnly: Read-only. To change who approves, assign a template to the companies, leave types and employees it should cover in the section above.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.scopesEmpty: No active approval rule narrows by business unit, department or position, and none carries steps of its own.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.chainEmptyFallback: No steps of its own — these requests fall back to the org-wide default flow.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.readoutHint: The flow a request for this leave type reaches when no narrower rule applies to the employee. Read-only — change it on Approval chain.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.sourceFallback: Built-in chain — no rule and no org-wide default
leaveConfigApprovalChains.escalationOn: Escalates after {days, plural, one {# working day} other {# working days}} to {target}.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.otherRules: {n, plural, one {# other rule} other {# other rules}} in this company can route this leave type differently, depending on the employee.
leaveConfigApprovalChains.candidateRules: {n, plural, one {# rule in this company is} other {# rules in this company are}} scoped to this leave type; the chain above is what applies when none of them matches.

scheduleConfig.pageSubtitle: What governs an employee's working pattern. Values are shown here and edited where they are stored.
scheduleConfig.notBuiltYet: This section has not been built yet. It is named here so the full shape is visible — it will be defined and built as its own piece of work.
scheduleConfig.shiftsHint: Every shift in the library, with the weekly pattern it applies. Rest is every weekday not marked Full, Half or Off.
scheduleConfig.shiftsEmpty: No shifts have been created yet.
scheduleConfig.noPattern: No weekly pattern set — this shift cannot generate a roster.
scheduleConfig.shiftLibraryLink: Open the shift library to add or edit a shift →
scheduleConfig.weekHint: The company schedule used for any day an employee has no shift assigned. It also decides which weekdays count as working days for absence and roster generation.
scheduleConfig.weekEmpty: No companies are in your scope.
scheduleConfig.workScheduleLink: Overtime rates, registered devices and backup-shift coverage →
scheduleConfig.groupHint: These settings belong to a Schedule Group — the named rule set every shift under it follows. Pick a group to see its settings.
scheduleConfig.groupEmpty: No Schedule Group has been set up yet.
scheduleConfig.graceHint: How long after the scheduled start, and before the scheduled end, {group} waits before a clocking counts as late or early.
scheduleConfig.recordRulesHint: Once the interval on the left has passed, the group records the number of minutes on the right against that day’s attendance.
scheduleConfig.notPayNote: These minutes are written on the attendance record only. Nothing in payroll reads them, so no payslip is reduced by them. Making them affect someone’s pay would be a separate decision, with its own before and after.
scheduleConfig.otEarlyHint: Whether time clocked before the scheduled start counts as overtime. There is no approval step behind it: with it on, every pre-shift minute becomes overtime.
scheduleConfig.otEarlyLabel: Count time clocked before the scheduled start as overtime
scheduleConfig.otRoundingHint: Each overtime band rounds on its own, so the first hour and the third hour can round differently.
scheduleConfig.otRoundingEmpty: This group has no overtime bands, so overtime is counted to the exact minute.
scheduleConfig.gapsHint: These were asked for on this tab. Each one is named rather than drawn as a control, because nothing behind it would save.
scheduleConfig.gapRotationBody: Not stored anywhere. A roster is generated in one go from a shift's weekly pattern over a date range; nothing records a repeating cycle that moves people on each week. A control for it would need storage that does not exist yet.
scheduleConfig.gapRosterBody: Fixed rules, not settings. Only an HR administrator may change a roster date that is today or earlier, and roster edits are restricted at the database. Neither can be turned off from a screen.
scheduleConfig.gapDayTypesTitle: Exception conditions that override a normal day
scheduleConfig.gapDayTypesBody: Only partly real. The five day types are fixed, and two of them — company holiday and shutdown day — are recorded but not yet acted on. Off day and rest day are treated as one non-working weekday. The setting that uses them belongs to leave counting, not to the schedule.
scheduleConfig.gapOtCapBody: Stored on the payroll policy, not on the schedule, and edited under Payroll. Shown there so one figure has one owner.
scheduleConfig.groupDeleteBody: It is removed for good. A group that a shift still uses cannot be deleted — move those shifts to another group first.
scheduleConfig.policyNoDelete: There is no Delete here, on purpose. Removing a company's setting would silently put that company back on the built-in defaults and switch the registered-device requirement off. Use Edit to change it.
scheduleConfig.wsOtHint: The overtime rates for your whole organisation, the devices employees registered for web clocking, and the employees who still have no backup shift.
scheduleConfig.listSubtitle: Every Schedule Group, and the tenant- and company-wide settings that belong to none of them. Open a group to see and change its own settings.
scheduleConfig.addSubtitle: Name the new Schedule Group and set the rules it carries. Its working week, grace periods and overtime rounding are set on its own page as soon as it exists.
scheduleConfig.groupGone: This Schedule Group is not on the list. It may have been deleted, or the link may be out of date.
scheduleConfig.generalViewHint: What this Schedule Group is called and whether it is in use.
scheduleConfig.weekSectionHint: Which days of the week this Schedule Group works. The group says which days; the shift says which hours.
scheduleConfig.weekRestNote: Rest is not stored: a day that is not full, half or off is a rest day.
scheduleConfig.weekNone: This Schedule Group declares no working week, so every shift under it keeps its own. That is the normal state, and it is what the Standard group must keep: a week here would be imposed on every shift that is in no group.
scheduleConfig.duplicatedToast: Schedule Group duplicated. You are on the copy.
scheduleConfig.deductionsHere: This switch is set in the General section at the top of this page, and only there. The date it starts from is stamped when you turn it on and can never be typed, so a payroll month you have already closed can never pick up a deduction afterwards.

leaveConfigLeaveCredit.pageDescription: Credits earned by working a rest day, off day or public holiday, and the Replacement Leave that uses them.

leaveCredit.moduleOffTitle: Leave Credit is not switched on for this account
leaveCredit.moduleOffBody: Leave Credit is a paid add-on. Turning it on is arranged separately; until then no credit can be earned, added or configured here.
leaveCredit.windDown: Leave Credit is not switched on for this account, so no new credit can be earned or added and the rules cannot be changed. {accruals} credit(s) are still outstanding: they are listed below and can still be expired, paid out or reversed.
leaveCredit.empty: No Leave Credit movements match these filters.
leaveCredit.truncated: Showing the {shown} most recent of {matched} movements. Narrow the filters to see older ones.
leaveCredit.reverseFootnote: Reversing never deletes a line. The original stays exactly as it was, marked Reversed, and a reversal line is added beside it. A credit that has already been used cannot be reversed; cancel the leave that used it first.
leaveCredit.orderFootnote: Before and After are the employee's running Replacement Leave balance, counted in date order and then in the order the lines were recorded. A line dated earlier than lines already recorded changes Before and After for every later line. The list shows the newest first.

reverse.title: Reverse this Leave Credit
reverse.body: The credit line stays, marked Reversed, and a reversal line is added. If overtime was recorded on the date worked, it becomes payable again.

banner.grantedOvertime: The {hours} hour(s) of overtime recorded on {date} will not also be paid.
banner.reversedOvertime: The {hours} hour(s) of overtime recorded on {date} are payable again.

add.title: Add Leave Credit
add.description: For a day an employee worked but did not send a request, and management agreed HR should credit it.
add.employeePlaceholder: Search by name or Employee ID
add.expiryHint: Filled in from your rule; you can change it. It cannot be before the date worked.
add.workingDay: This is an ordinary working day for this employee. Only a rest day, off day or public holiday can earn a Leave Credit.
add.overtime: This date already has {hours} hour(s) of overtime recorded for this employee. Once credited, that overtime will not also be paid, because the day is being given back as leave instead.
add.alreadyCredited: This employee already has a Leave Credit for this date.
add.policyOff: Leave Credit is switched off for this employee's company. Switch it on in the Rules tab first.
add.firstScheduleConsent: This employee is within the First Schedule, so statutory overtime pay applies. A credit needs their recorded agreement to take leave instead of that pay, and any credit they do not use will be paid out when it expires.
add.firstScheduleConsentLabel: The employee has agreed to take this day as leave instead of statutory overtime pay.
add.firstScheduleBlocked: This employee is within the First Schedule and their company does not allow a Leave Credit in place of statutory overtime pay. Change that in the Rules tab first.
add.extendedShort: This is an ordinary working day. Only {minutes} minute(s) past the scheduled shift end counted for this employee, which is below the company’s half-day threshold, so this date cannot earn a Leave Credit.
add.extendedEarned: This employee worked {minutes} counted minute(s) past the scheduled shift end, which earns {days} day. The credit amount is fixed at that figure and cannot be changed here.

leaveCredit.rulesIntro: Who can earn a Leave Credit, how it is earned and how long a credit lasts, per company. A change here applies to credits granted after it; a credit already granted keeps its expiry date.

systemTesting.title: System Testing
systemTesting.description: The written checks this system is run through, and what happened each time one was run.
systemTesting.progressNote: Failing counts a case whose most recent run failed — not one that failed at some point in the past.
systemTesting.newDescription: Write the script once. Record what happens each time you run it on the case itself.
systemTesting.stepsHint: One step per line, in the order they are carried out.
systemTesting.detailDescription: The script, and every time it has been run.
systemTesting.recordRunNote: Each run is kept, so a test that passed in September and failed in October reads as two records rather than one.
systemTesting.runHistoryNote: Newest first. A run that did not pass can be raised on the feedback board without re-typing anything.
systemTesting.noRuns: This test has not been run yet.
systemTesting.viewRequest: Open the request this run raised

leaveConfigHistoryImport.pageDescription: Load past leave records from a file so they appear in each employee’s leave history. Balances are not changed.

leaveHistoryImport.dropHere: Drop an Excel file here, or click to choose one
leaveHistoryImport.uploadHint: Excel (.xlsx, .xls) or CSV, up to 5 MB. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
leaveHistoryImport.unsupportedFileType: That file type cannot be read. Use .xlsx, .xls or .csv.
leaveHistoryImport.fileTooLarge: That file is too large. Split it and upload the parts separately.
leaveHistoryImport.emptySheet: The first sheet of that workbook is empty.
leaveHistoryImport.fileReadError: That file could not be read.
leaveHistoryImport.csvPlaceholder: Paste the header row and the leave records here
leaveHistoryImport.columnReference: Which columns the file must have
leaveHistoryImport.columnHint: Employee No., Leave Reference, Leave Code, Leave Start Date, Leave End Date and Number of Day are required. The rest are kept when you supply them.
leaveHistoryImport.missingColumns: The file is missing {count} required column(s):
leaveHistoryImport.nothingSilentlyDropped: Rows in error and duplicates are not imported, and are never silently dropped.
leaveHistoryImport.resultTruncated: The report lists the first {shown} rejected rows of {total}.
leaveHistoryImport.noBalanceTitle: No leave balance moves — RETIRED (item 073233bb): whether a balance moves is now the uploader's per-run choice. Replaced by effectDeductTitle / effectNetTitle.
leaveHistoryImport.noBalanceBody: RETIRED (item 073233bb). This asserted that “the balances you migrate already have this leave removed from them”, which is a claim about the customer’s data that the product never asked about and cannot verify — and it is false whenever entitlement comes from the entitlement tables with nothing brought forward. Replaced by effectDeductBody / effectNetBody, which state what the chosen option does.
leaveHistoryImport.netQuestion: Are the balances you are starting from already net of this leave?
leaveHistoryImport.netQuestionHint: One answer for the whole file. It decides whether these records come off each person’s balance. Change it and the preview below is worked out again.
leaveHistoryImport.netNoLabel: No — my balances are the full allowance for the year
leaveHistoryImport.netNoHint: The allowances came from this system’s entitlement tables and nothing has been taken off them yet. Each record will deduct its days, exactly as an approved leave application does.
leaveHistoryImport.netYesLabel: Yes — my balances already have this leave taken out
leaveHistoryImport.netYesHint: You are bringing closing balances across from another system. The records are loaded and no balance moves, because deducting again would take the same days twice.
leaveHistoryImport.effectDeductTitle: These records will come off the balance
leaveHistoryImport.effectDeductBody: Each imported record deducts its days from the employee’s balance in the same step that creates the record, so Taken, Balance and the unused-leave figure at resignation all agree with the records behind them. Cancelling an imported record gives its days back, like any other leave. Change the answer above if the balances you are starting from already have this leave taken out of them.
leaveHistoryImport.effectNetBody: You have told us the balances you are starting from already have this leave taken out of them, so the records are loaded and nobody’s balance changes — deducting again would take the same days twice. These records will therefore not appear in the Taken figure on the balance screens, and cancelling one gives nothing back, because nothing was ever taken. Loading balances is the other tool’s job: Leave Adjustments › Leave Balance Import.
leaveHistoryImport.impactTitle: What this will do to each balance
leaveHistoryImport.impactHint: Worked out from the records that will be imported and each balance as it stands now. Nothing is written until you confirm.
leaveHistoryImport.impactNoneHint: Nothing. You have told us the balances you are starting from already have this leave taken out, so no balance will change.
leaveHistoryImport.impactNegativeWarning: {count} line(s) would take a balance below zero. That happens when the employee has not earned those days yet — look at the marked line(s) before you confirm.
leaveHistoryImport.impactPooledFrom: Filed under {codes}, deducted from this balance
leaveHistoryImport.historyHint: Every run, so you can answer “who loaded this, and when” months later. The uploaded file itself is not kept.
leaveHistoryImport.historyNoDetail: No per-row detail was kept for this run.

leaveBfImport.dropHere: Drop an Excel file here, or click to choose one
leaveBfImport.uploadHint: Excel (.xlsx, .xls) or CSV, up to 5 MB. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
leaveBfImport.unsupportedFileType: That file type cannot be read. Use .xlsx, .xls or .csv.
leaveBfImport.fileTooLarge: That file is too large. Split it and upload the parts separately.
leaveBfImport.emptySheet: The first sheet of that workbook is empty.
leaveBfImport.fileReadError: That file could not be read.
leaveBfImport.columnReference: Which columns the file must have
leaveBfImport.missingColumns: The file is missing {count} required column(s):
leaveBfImport.resultTruncated: The report lists the first {shown} rejected rows of {total}.
leaveBfImport.historyNoDetail: No per-row detail was kept for this run.
leaveBfImport.impactPooledFrom: Filed under {codes}, deducted from this balance
leaveBfImport.yearMeaning: Entitlement Year is the year the days go INTO. 2026 means days carried from 2025 into 2026. The system works out the date for each employee, so the file does not need one.
leaveBfImport.csvPlaceholder: Paste the header row and the brought-forward figures here
leaveBfImport.columnHint: Employee ID, Leave Code, Entitlement Year and B/F Days are required. Remark is kept when you supply it and appears against the entry.
leaveBfImport.nothingSilentlyDropped: Rows in error are not imported, and are never silently dropped.
leaveBfImport.resultNoRecord: No leave record was created, and no leave was deducted.
leaveBfImport.sequenceTitle: The order to load a migration in
leaveBfImport.sequence1: Generate the leave year’s entitlements first.
leaveBfImport.sequence3: Load the leave taken, on Leave History Data Import.
leaveBfImport.sequence4: Spot-check five to ten employees against their own Leave Balance.
leaveBfImport.modeQuestion: What should the figures in the file do?
leaveBfImport.modeQuestionHint: Changing this re-checks the file, so the effect shown below always belongs to the answer above.

replace.label: Replace (recommended)
replace.hint: The figure in the file becomes the brought-forward figure. It removes only what a previous B/F import put there — never leave, accruals or adjustments recorded any other way.

add.label: Add to existing
add.hint: The figure in the file is added to whatever is already brought forward.

modeReadout.replace: Replace: each figure below replaces what a previous B/F import put there.
modeReadout.add: Add to existing: each figure below is added to what is already brought forward.

leaveBfImport.impactTitle: What Brought Forward will read afterwards
leaveBfImport.impactHint: Brought Forward is the figure before the carry rule; Carried Forward is what the balance screen shows after it. Where they differ, the difference is forfeited.
leaveBfImport.impactNoneHint: No line in this file would change a balance.
leaveBfImport.impactCappedWarning: {count} figure(s) are above the leave type’s carry-forward limit. The excess is forfeited, as shown.
leaveBfImport.historyHint: Every run, so you can answer “who loaded this, and when” months later, and roll one back if the file was wrong. The uploaded file itself is not kept.
leaveBfImport.rollbackHint: Rolling back writes the reversing entries rather than deleting anything, so the record of what was loaded and what undid it survives.

leaveConfigBfImport.pageDescription: Load the brought-forward days a leave year opens with, from a file. No leave record is created and no leave is deducted.

leaveDataImport.wrongType: This file does not match the selected Import Type. Change the selection in Step 1 or download its template.

onboarding.welcomeBody: A quick 30-second tour of where everything lives. You can replay it any time from the help button in the top bar.
onboarding.navBody: Every module lives in this sidebar. What you see here depends on your role — employees, managers and HR admins each get their own tools.
onboarding.workspaceBody: Your personal hub: profile, payslips, leave balance and attendance — everything about you, in one place.
onboarding.kbBody: Step-by-step guides for every module, plus your company’s policies and documents. Start here whenever you’re unsure how something works.
onboarding.approvalsBody: As a manager, requests from your team — leave, attendance and profile changes — wait for your decision here.
onboarding.adminBody: Set up your company, departments and people, configure leave and payroll, manage roles, and review the audit trail. New here? Open the “Getting Started” guide in the Knowledge Base.
onboarding.languageBody: Use the app in English, 简体中文, Bahasa Melayu, தமிழ், ไทย or Tiếng Việt — your choice is remembered.
onboarding.themeBody: Toggle between light and dark themes to suit your eyes and your room.
onboarding.finishBody: That’s the tour. Whenever you need a hand, open the Knowledge Base or replay this tour from the help button.

intro.title: Your self-service home
intro.body: This is your personal hub. We'll walk through your profile, bank and statutory details, payslips, and your leave and attendance summary.

contact.title: Your contact details
contact.body: Update your phone, address, date of birth, and emergency contact here. These changes save **immediately**, no approval needed.

bank.title: Bank and statutory
bank.body: Your bank account and PCB tax category live here. Open **Request a change** to submit edits, which go to your admin for approval.

payslips.title: Your payslips
payslips.body: Every pay period lands here. Click a period to open the full payslip and download it.

attendance.title: Attendance summary
attendance.body: Check in and out for today from here. For your full attendance history, open the Attendance page. You can also request a fix for a missed punch.

leave.title: Leave balances and requests
leave.body: See what's accrued, used, and available across leave types. Use **Request leave** to file a new application.

intro.title: Leave walkthrough
intro.body: Welcome to Leave. We'll show you your leave balances, how to request time off, and where requests are tracked.

balance.title: Check your balance
balance.body: This table shows how much leave you have left, broken down by type. Available days appear over your total entitlement.

request.title: Request leave
request.body: Open this panel to fill in the dates, leave type, and reason, then submit your request for approval.

config.title: Configure leave types
config.body: Admins set up leave types, entitlements, and the leave year here. This is where policies and holidays are managed.

intro.title: Tour the attendance page
intro.body: This quick walkthrough covers checking in and out, reading daily status, your record, and submitting a correction request.

day.title: Your daily record
day.body: This card lists everyone for the selected day, with check-in, check-out, hours, and overtime. Use the date nav up top to move between days.

action.title: Check in and out
action.body: Each row's action enters a time and **checks you in**, then later **checks you out**. Once both are set, the day is marked done.

status.title: Present, late, half day
status.body: The status pill shows present, late, half day, or absent for the day. On leave, holidays, and rest days appear here too.

correction.title: Request a correction
correction.body: Wrong time logged? Submit a correction request with the proposed times and a reason, then a manager approves or rejects it.

summary.title: Your monthly summary
summary.body: Scroll down for the month roll-up: present, late, half day, leave, absent days, plus hours and overtime flags. That wraps up the tour.

intro.title: Run a payroll cycle
intro.body: This walkthrough covers running payroll: creating a payroll process, reviewing payroll processes, and finding statutory reports like EA and CP39.

batches.title: Your payroll processes
batches.body: Every pay run lives here. Click a period to open a payroll process and review payslips, net pay, and statutory totals.

create.title: Create Payroll Run Cycle
create.body: Click **Create Payroll Run Cycle** to open the guided wizard: pick the period and cycle, choose employees, then review and process.

reports.title: Statutory reports
reports.body: This is where EA, Form E, CP39, and monthly EPF/SOCSO/EIS statutory reports are generated.

worklist.title: Compliance worklist
worklist.body: Track CP22 and CP22A obligations here so new hires and leavers are notified to LHDN on time.

generate.title: Generate a report
generate.body: Choose a company, report, and period, then click **Preview** to review figures before exporting or recording.

intro.title: People and org tour
intro.body: This quick walkthrough shows you how to find people, hire, and manage your organization's master data. Let's start on the People page.

search.title: Search for people
search.body: Type a name or email here and hit **Search** to filter the directory. Use **Clear** to reset back to everyone.

table.title: Browse the directory
table.body: Every employee shows here with their department, company, and status. Click a name to open their full profile.

hire.title: Create new employee
hire.body: Click **+ Create new employee** at the top right. It opens a step-by-step screen — you can save a draft at any point and finish it later. For bulk onboarding, use **Import employees** with the Excel template.

orgTree.title: Your group structure
orgTree.body: Admins manage org master data here. This tree shows how your companies nest into a group.

orgCompanies.title: Companies and master data
orgCompanies.body: Open any company to manage its details, statutory identity, and bank profiles. Use **Add company** below to register a new one. The shared lists — departments, positions, cost centers — now live under System Labels.

intro.title: System Labels
intro.body: This is where you set up the shared lists everyone else picks from — departments, positions, cost centers and business units for each company, plus your organisation-wide grades.

companies.title: Per-company catalogs
companies.body: Open a company to add, edit, archive or delete its departments, positions, cost centers and business units. Each can carry an optional description. Grades are organisation-wide and are maintained from the same screen.

intro.title: Performance reviews tour
intro.body: This quick walkthrough shows how to run performance review cycles, handle reviews awaiting you, and open or create a cycle.

pending.title: Reviews awaiting you
pending.body: When team reviews need your input they appear here. Click **Review** on any row to complete it.

cycles.title: Review cycles
cycles.body: Every cycle is listed here with its period, status, and progress. Click a cycle name to open it and manage its reviews.

newCycle.title: Create a new cycle
newCycle.body: Expand this panel to set the name, scope, period, and merit pool, then click **Create cycle** to launch it.

intro.title: Your approvals inbox
intro.body: This is the one place where everything awaiting your decision lands — leave, attendance corrections and profile changes. Let's walk through how to clear it.

header.title: Pending at a glance
header.body: The header shows how many requests are still pending across all queues. When it hits zero, your inbox is clear.

leave.title: Leave requests
leave.body: Each pending leave request shows the employee, type, dates and days. Review the details before you decide.

decide.title: Approve or reject
decide.body: Use the buttons in this column to **approve** or **reject** a request. You can't approve your own — those rows show *Your request* instead.

corrections.title: Attendance corrections
corrections.body: Punch-time fixes appear here. RLS already trims every queue to what you're allowed to see, so you only decide within your scope.

intro.title: Tour the org chart
intro.body: This quick walkthrough shows how to **search**, **collapse and zoom**, and read the reporting lines that connect your team.

header.title: Your org at a glance
header.body: The header names this view and shows how many people are mapped. Everyone reports up from here.

search.title: Find anyone fast
search.body: Type a name, role, or department in the **search** box at the top right. Matches light up and scroll into view, even inside collapsed branches.

controls.title: Collapse and zoom
controls.body: Click the **+/− toggle** under any manager to collapse or expand their reports. Use the **zoom buttons** to fit large teams on screen.

lines.title: Read the reporting lines
lines.body: Each connector style means a different relationship. Check this **legend** to tell direct, functional, project, and dotted-line reporting apart.

intro.title: Admin walkthrough
intro.body: This tour covers managing user roles, assigning and revoking access, scoped company admins, and the audit trail. Let's start with users.

users.title: Your users
users.body: Every person in the system is listed here with their current roles. Each tag shows a role and, when scoped, the company it applies to.

assign.title: Assign a role
assign.body: Pick a role, optionally scope it to a company, then click **Add role**. Use the **×** beside a tag to revoke access.

provisioning.title: Scoped admins
provisioning.body: Company-scoped **hr_admin** roles let delegated admins manage only their own subtree. This note explains how provisioning and scope work.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: Now jump to the audit log. Filter by record type, search events, or narrow a date range to find exactly what changed.

auditTable.title: Every change, logged
auditTable.body: Each row is one event from the immutable log — who did what, when. That's the admin tour; you're all set.

claims.title: Claims
claims.subtitle: Submit an expense or benefit claim and track its status.
claims.noTypes: No claim types are configured yet. Ask your HR admin to add them.
claims.cancelConfirmDescription: This withdraws the claim. You can submit a new one.
claims.noEmployment: No active employment is linked to your account, so you cannot submit claims.
claims.draftHint: A draft holds none of your claim limit until you submit it.
claims.draftsHint: Saved but not yet submitted. Tick the ones you want to file and submit them together.
claims.submitSelectedHint: All selected drafts are submitted together, or none are.
claims.deleteDraftConfirmDescription: The draft and any receipt attached to it are removed. This cannot be undone.
claims.mileagePricedOnSubmit: The amount is worked out from the mileage rate table when you submit.

analytics.title: HR analytics
analytics.description: Headcount, hiring, attrition and master-data exports for the selected period.
analytics.turnoverFormula: Turnover rate = leavers ÷ average headcount × 100. Average headcount = (start + end) / 2.
analytics.masterDataDesc: Download the active employee roster. Compensation columns are admin-only.
analytics.pdfNonLatinNote: PDF is a human-readable summary; non-Latin names (e.g. CJK, Tamil) appear as “?”. Use Excel or CSV for the lossless export.
analytics.sickNotConfigured: No sick-leave type is configured for this tenant.
analytics.nationalityFootnote: Nationality uses EPF citizenship as a proxy; it defaults to Citizen when unset.
analytics.carryForwardDesc: Annual-leave amounts brought forward into each leave year, their expiry date, and what was forfeited — at year/cycle open (exceeded the carry-forward limit) and at expiry (unused brought-forward days lapsed).

payComponents.title: Pay Items
payComponents.description: Define configurable pay items and their statutory treatment (EPF / SOCSO / PCB / HRDF).
payComponents.previewNotice: Preview. The catalog is ready to use; payroll switches to typed components only when enabled (TYPED_PAY_COMPONENTS_ENABLED). Until then payroll runs on basic + allowance + overtime + bonus as today.
payComponents.archiveDescription: Deactivate {code}? It will no longer be available to add — you can reactivate it later.
payComponents.empty: No pay items found — adjust the search/filter, or seed the Malaysia defaults to start.
payComponents.flagsHint: Flags decide which statutory base the component feeds. Non-Payable items and PCB-only earnings are not computed in this version.
payComponents.epfConfigTip: Controls how this pay code feeds the EPF (KWSP) contribution. EPF Bonus 2012 marks it as a bonus payment under the EPF bonus contribution rules.
payComponents.epfBonus2012Tip: Treat this pay code as a bonus payment for EPF: the amount is added to the month's wage and the EPF statutory table is read once for the total, so the employer rate follows the whole month (EPF Bonus 2012 rules). Requires EPF to be ticked.
payComponents.pcbConfigTip: Classifies this pay code for Monthly Tax Deduction per the LHDN Spesifikasi Pengiraan PCB 2026 Menggunakan Pengiraan Berkomputer.
payComponents.remunerationTypeTip: How the pay code enters the PCB calculation (LHDN PCB 2026 specification): Normal remuneration, Additional remuneration, or an Optional Deduction that reduces the monthly tax.
payComponents.exemptionTypeTip: The LHDN exemption or optional-deduction code with its yearly limit (RM). The list follows the selected Remuneration Type: PCB codes for Normal/Additional, LP codes for Optional Deduction.
payComponents.errorStatutory_pcbRemunerationTypeRequir: Remuneration Type is required when PCB is ticked.
payComponents.errorStatutory_pcbExemptionTypeRequired: Exemption Type is required when PCB is ticked.
payComponents.errorStatutory_pcbExemptionTypeInvalid: The selected Exemption Type does not belong to the chosen Remuneration Type.
payComponents.errorStatutory_epfBonusRequiresEpf: EPF Bonus 2012 requires the pay code to be subject to EPF.
payComponents.errorUnsupportedTaxable: Pay code "{code}" has no supported taxable classification. Select the applicable benefit Pay Category and tax settings before saving.
payComponents.errorBenefit_classification_conflict: Pay code "{code}" has conflicting BIK and living accommodation classifications. Make Pay Category and EA reporting consistent.
payComponents.errorBenefit_unsupported_kind: Pay code "{code}" uses a category that cannot represent a non-cash benefit. Review its Category and Pay Category.
payComponents.errorBenefit_normal_remuneration_require: Pay code "{code}": monthly BIK and living accommodation require Normal remuneration and cannot use EPF Bonus 2012.
payComponents.benefitRemunerationHint: Monthly BIK and living accommodation use Normal remuneration for PCB. Pay Category identifies the benefit; EA reporting remains separate.
payComponents.recordOnlyNote: Record only — does not affect take-home pay.
payComponents.sectionEaFormHint: Where this pay item's money is reported on the C.P.8A (EA). It changes no calculation and no statutory flag. The EA form itself says which years a mapping is not yet in effect for.
payComponents.deleteDescription: Permanently delete {code}. Blocked if any employee or payroll run uses it — deactivate instead.
payComponents.searchPlaceholder: Search pay code, label or description…
payComponents.errorInUse: This pay item is used by {refs} record(s) — deactivate it instead of deleting.
payComponents.errorCodeDuplicate: Pay code {code} already exists — pay codes must be unique.
payComponents.errorCodeDuplicateArchived: Pay code {code} exists but is deactivated — reactivate it instead.
payComponents.inputTypeLinkTitle: Open {code} to change its Input Type
payComponents.sectionPaySettingsHint: How the amount is worked out — rounding, Input Type and the Formula builder.
payComponents.displayCategoryHint: For cash items, Payroll Category controls where the item is shown. For non-payable benefits, choose BIK or VOLA; Subject to PCB determines whether the benefit enters taxable remuneration. EA reporting is configured separately.
payComponents.sectionOrpHint: Choose whether this pay item is included when the ordinary rate of pay is worked out. The two boxes are independent — tick either, both or neither. The ORP formula itself is unchanged; these boxes only decide which pay items feed it.
payComponents.orpUnpaidLeaveLabel: Add to Unpaid Leave ORP Calculation
payComponents.orpUnpaidLeaveHint: Today the unpaid-leave and absence daily rate is worked out from basic salary alone. Tick this to add this pay item to that base. It also lowers the EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and HRDF bases, because the unpaid-leave deduction is taken before those are worked out.
payComponents.orpOvertimeHint: Counts this pay item towards the "All fixed allowances" total your overtime formula reads. Until now that was decided by the item’s Category instead; every item was ticked on release day so nobody’s overtime changed.
payComponents.orpDeductionWarning: This pay item is a Deduction. Malaysian employment law works overtime out from the ordinary rate of pay derived from wages, so a deduction is not taken off that base. Your choice is saved, but it does not lower anyone’s overtime or unpaid-leave rate. Tell us if you need this to change.
payComponents.orpStatutoryNote: Statutory overtime worked out from attendance is not affected by these boxes. It is based on the Basic Salary and Monthly Allowance on the employee’s Personnel record.
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B1A: B1 (a) Gross salary, wages or leave pay (including overtime pay)
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B1B: B1 (b) Fees (including director fees), commission or bonus
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B1C: B1 (c) Gross tips, perquisites, awards / rewards or other allowances
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B1D: B1 (d) Income tax borne by the employer in respect of his employee
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B1E: B1 (e) Employee Share Option Scheme (ESOS) benefit
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B4: B4 - Value of living accommodation provided
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B5: B5 - Refund from unapproved Provident / Pension Fund
payComponents.eaLine_EA_B6: B6 - Compensation for loss of employment
payComponents.eaLine_EA_C2: C2 - Annuities or other periodical payments

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.ariaBell: Notifications, {total} waiting: {unread} unread and {tasks} open tasks
